theorems.name: critAll
theorems.areas: zeta and L-series, Dirichlet and multiplicative characters

a.states: For every positive integer N, every primitive complex Dirichlet character χ modulo N and every complex number s with 0 < Re s < 1, if the Dirichlet L-function L(s, χ) vanishes at s, then Re s = 1/2. Here L(s, χ) is Mathlib's analytic continuation of the Dirichlet series of χ, and for N = 1 it is the Riemann zeta function. The statement is therefore the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions in the open critical strip, and it contains the Riemann Hypothesis as the case N = 1.
a.notation: ∀ N ≥ 1, ∀ primitive χ mod N, ∀ s ∈ ℂ, (0 < Re s < 1 ∧ L(s, χ) = 0) ⇒ Re s = 1/2
a.known_as: the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, an open conjecture that has no accepted published proof
a.reference: Harold Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory, 3rd edition revised by Hugh L. Montgomery, 2000
a.vacuity: None found, since the known zeros such as s = 1/2 + 14.1347i for N = 1 meet every hypothesis, and the primitivity hypothesis, whose Lean name begins with an underscore and is therefore apparently unused, could be dropped without changing the content because the extra Euler factors of an imprimitive character vanish only on the line Re s = 0.
a.why: The Lean text matches the textbook form of the conjecture term by term, so the reading is certain, while a proof of this open problem would be extraordinary and calls for an audit of the axioms and the trust base of the project.

b.states: For every positive modulus N, every primitive complex Dirichlet character χ of modulus N and every complex number s with 0 < Re s < 1, if the Mathlib Dirichlet L-function L(χ, s) vanishes at s, then Re s = 1/2. The trivial character of modulus 1 is primitive and its L-function is the Riemann zeta function, so the statement contains the Riemann hypothesis.
b.known_as: the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, which is an open conjecture and not a published theorem
b.vacuity: None found, since the known zeros in the critical strip meet the hypotheses, and the primitivity hypothesis, whose underscore name marks it as unused, can be dropped because the extra Euler factors of an imprimitive L-function vanish only on the line Re s = 0.

check.known_as: the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, an open conjecture with no accepted published proof
check.vacuity: None found, since for N = 1 the first nontrivial zero 1/2 + 14.1347…i of the Riemann zeta function meets every hypothesis.
check.note: The statement is an open conjecture, so a claimed proof of it calls for a check of the axioms and of any unproved assumptions behind its 800,343 declarations, and the primitivity hypothesis has an underscore name, which in Lean marks a hypothesis that the proof leaves unused.

theorems.name: riemannHypothesis
theorems.areas: zeta and L-series

a.states: The theorem asserts Mathlib's proposition RiemannHypothesis. That proposition says that every complex number s with ζ(s) = 0 that is not one of the trivial zeros −2, −4, −6, … and differs from 1 has real part 1/2. Here ζ is Mathlib's Riemann zeta function, the meromorphic continuation of the sum of n^(−s), to which Mathlib also assigns a finite value at the pole s = 1.
a.known_as: the Riemann Hypothesis, an open conjecture that has no accepted published proof
a.reference: Bernhard Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse, 1859
a.vacuity: None found, since the known zeros such as 1/2 + 14.1347i meet every hypothesis, and the condition s ≠ 1 is redundant but harmless because Mathlib's value of ζ at 1 is nonzero.
a.why: Mathlib's definition is the textbook statement of the Riemann Hypothesis, so the reading is certain, while a proof of this open problem would be extraordinary and calls for an audit of the axioms and the trust base of the project.

b.states: The statement is the Mathlib proposition RiemannHypothesis. It says that every complex number s with riemannZeta s = 0, s not of the form −2(n + 1) for a natural number n, and s ≠ 1 has real part 1/2. Here riemannZeta is the meromorphic continuation of the Riemann zeta function, with a value assigned at the pole s = 1.
b.known_as: the Riemann hypothesis, an open conjecture and one of the Millennium Prize Problems, not a published theorem
b.vacuity: None found, and the side condition s ≠ 1 removes only the pole, where the value (γ − log 4π)/2 that Mathlib assigns is nonzero anyway.

check.known_as: the Riemann Hypothesis, an open conjecture and one of the Millennium Prize Problems, with no accepted published proof
check.vacuity: None found, and the side condition s ≠ 1 is redundant because the value (γ − log 4π)/2 that Mathlib assigns to ζ at 1 is nonzero.
check.note: The statement is an open conjecture, so a claimed proof of it calls for a check of the axioms and of any unproved assumptions behind its 800,342 declarations.

theorems.name: rhOfAll
theorems.areas: zeta and L-series

a.states: The theorem asserts Mathlib's proposition RiemannHypothesis, exactly as theorem 2 does. That proposition says that every complex number s with ζ(s) = 0 that is not one of the trivial zeros −2, −4, −6, … and differs from 1 has real part 1/2.
a.known_as: the Riemann Hypothesis, an open conjecture that has no accepted published proof
a.reference: Bernhard Riemann, Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse, 1859
a.vacuity: None found, since the known zeros such as 1/2 + 14.1347i meet every hypothesis, and the condition s ≠ 1 is redundant but harmless because Mathlib's value of ζ at 1 is nonzero.
a.why: The statement is the same Mathlib proposition as in theorem 2, and its name and its place in the module of theorem 1 suggest that it is obtained from theorem 1 by taking N = 1 and adding the zeros outside the critical strip.

b.states: The statement is again the Mathlib proposition RiemannHypothesis. It claims that every zero of riemannZeta other than the trivial zeros −2, −4, −6 and so on, and other than the point s = 1, has real part 1/2. Its text is identical to that of theorem 2, and only its name and module differ.
b.known_as: the Riemann hypothesis, an open conjecture and one of the Millennium Prize Problems, not a published theorem
b.vacuity: None found, and the side condition s ≠ 1 removes only the pole, where the value that Mathlib assigns is nonzero anyway.

check.known_as: the Riemann Hypothesis, an open conjecture and one of the Millennium Prize Problems, with no accepted published proof
check.vacuity: None found, and the side condition s ≠ 1 is redundant because the value (γ − log 4π)/2 that Mathlib assigns to ζ at 1 is nonzero.
check.note: The Lean text is word for word that of theorem 2, so the two entries record one claim under two names and in two modules.

theorems.name: PositivityTheory.KB.PrincipalPrimes.exists_prime
theorems.areas: number fields, ring theory

a.states: For every number field L and every natural number B, there is a prime element π of the ring of integers 𝒪_L such that the absolute norm of the principal ideal π𝒪_L, which is the index of π𝒪_L in 𝒪_L, is at least B. Since only finitely many ideals of 𝒪_L have norm below a given bound, the statement says that 𝒪_L has infinitely many principal prime ideals.
a.notation: ∀ number field L, ∀ B ∈ ℕ, ∃ π ∈ 𝒪_L prime with N(π𝒪_L) ≥ B
a.known_as: the infinitude of principal prime ideals, the case of the trivial class in the theorem that every ideal class of a number field contains infinitely many prime ideals
a.reference: Jürgen Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter VII §13, 1999
a.vacuity: None found, since B is arbitrary and a prime element always generates a nonzero prime ideal of norm at least 2.
a.why: The content follows at once from the density theorem for ideal classes, which gives density 1/h to the principal primes, but whether the version with a bound B counts as a standard fact or as a technical step is a judgment.

b.states: For every number field L and every natural number B there is a prime element π of the ring of integers of L whose principal ideal has absolute norm at least B. Only finitely many prime ideals have norm below a given bound, so the statement says that the ring of integers of L has infinitely many principal prime ideals.
b.known_as: the infinitude of principal prime ideals in a number field, which is the case of the trivial class in Weber's theorem that every ideal class contains infinitely many prime ideals and which also follows from the Chebotarev density theorem for the Hilbert class field

check.known_as: the theorem that every ideal class of a number field contains infinitely many prime ideals, in the case of the principal class
check.note: The norm bound B expresses infinitude because only finitely many ideals have norm below a bound, and the proof needs class field theory, since a prime ideal of L is principal exactly when it splits completely in the Hilbert class field of L.

theorems.name: PositivityTheory.KB.PrincipalPrimes.exists_principal
theorems.areas: number fields, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: For every number field L and every finite set T of nonzero prime ideals of 𝒪_L, there is a nonzero prime ideal of 𝒪_L outside T that is principal. Mathlib's HeightOneSpectrum of the Dedekind domain 𝒪_L is the set of its nonzero prime ideals. The statement is thus another form of the infinitude of principal prime ideals of 𝒪_L.
a.notation: ∀ number field L, ∀ finite set T of nonzero primes of 𝒪_L, ∃ nonzero prime 𝔭 ∉ T with 𝔭 principal
a.known_as: the infinitude of principal prime ideals, the case of the trivial class in the theorem that every ideal class of a number field contains infinitely many prime ideals
a.reference: Jürgen Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter VII §13, 1999
a.why: The content equals that of theorem 4 and follows at once from the density theorem for ideal classes, while the choice between standard fact and technical step is a judgment.

b.states: For every number field L and every finite set T of height-one primes of the ring of integers of L there is a height-one prime v outside T whose ideal is principal. This says that the ring of integers has infinitely many principal nonzero prime ideals, which is the same content as theorem 4.
b.known_as: the infinitude of principal prime ideals in a number field, which is the case of the trivial class in Weber's theorem that every ideal class contains infinitely many prime ideals

check.known_as: the theorem that every ideal class of a number field contains infinitely many prime ideals, in the case of the principal class
check.note: The statement has the same content as theorem 4, with a finite set of excluded primes in place of the norm bound.

theorems.name: UpperTheory.V.FW.embed
theorems.areas: number fields, linear algebra, field theory

a.states: For every prime l and every number field K that is Galois over ℚ with abelian Galois group, there are natural numbers f and D with f > 1 and f prime to l such that the following holds for all natural numbers n and n₀. For every field K′ that is the extension of K generated by the l^n-th roots of unity, there are a natural number m ≥ n₀, a field L isomorphic to the cyclotomic field ℚ(ζ_{f·l^m}) and a field embedding of K′ into L such that the degree of L over K′ is at most D·l^{n₀}. In words, the cyclotomic l-tower over K lies inside the fields ℚ(ζ_{f·l^m}) for one fixed level f prime to l, with a relative degree bounded independently of n.
a.notation: ∀ prime l, ∀ abelian number field K, ∃ f, D ∈ ℕ with f > 1 and gcd(f, l) = 1, ∀ n, n₀ ∈ ℕ, ∃ m ≥ n₀, ∃ embedding K(μ_{l^n}) ↪ L = ℚ(μ_{f·l^m}) with dim_{K(μ_{l^n})} L ≤ D·l^{n₀}
a.known_as: a consequence of the Kronecker–Weber theorem that places the cyclotomic l-tower of an abelian field inside the cyclotomic fields ℚ(ζ_{f·l^m}) with f prime to l, as in the setup of the Ferrero–Washington theorem
a.reference: Lawrence C. Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, 2nd edition, 1997
a.vacuity: None found, since the requirement f > 1 can always be met by multiplying the prime-to-l part of the conductor of K by a prime other than l, and the field K(μ_{l^n}) meets the hypothesis on K′ for every n.
a.why: The statement follows from the Kronecker–Weber theorem by taking m as the largest of n, n₀ and the exponent of l in the conductor of K, but its shape with two indices n and n₀ matches no textbook statement and serves a specific proof.

b.states: Take any prime l and any number field K that is abelian Galois over ℚ. Then there are natural numbers f and D, with f coprime to l and f > 1, that work for all natural numbers n and n₀ in the following way. Every number field K' that is the cyclotomic extension of K by the l^n-th roots of unity embeds into the cyclotomic field ℚ(ζ_{f·l^m}) for some natural number m ≥ n₀. The degree of that cyclotomic field over K' is at most D·l^{n₀}.
b.known_as: a consequence of the Kronecker–Weber theorem with conductors, saying that the cyclotomic l-tower over an abelian field lies with bounded index in the cyclotomic tower ℚ(ζ_{f·l^m}) of a fixed tame level f, the reduction used in the proof of the Ferrero–Washington theorem
b.vacuity: None found, but the bound D·l^{n₀} is generous and leaves as the real content the existence of an embedding whose tame level f does not depend on n.

check.known_as: the Kronecker–Weber theorem, in a form that is uniform along the cyclotomic l-tower over an abelian field and uses one level f prime to l
check.note: Taking n = n₀ = 0 makes K′ equal to K, so the statement contains the Kronecker–Weber theorem for K itself and the relation weaker that both readers give understates it, while the uniformity in n follows from that theorem by counting degrees of cyclotomic fields.

theorems.name: UpperTheory.V.CF.kwHom
theorems.areas: number fields, field theory

a.states: For every number field L that is Galois over ℚ with abelian Galois group, there are a positive integer N and a homomorphism of ℚ-algebras from L to the cyclotomic field ℚ(ζ_N). Such a homomorphism is injective because L is a field, so every abelian number field embeds into a cyclotomic field.
a.notation: ∀ number field L with L/ℚ abelian, ∃ N ≥ 1, ∃ ℚ-embedding L ↪ ℚ(ζ_N)
a.known_as: the Kronecker–Weber theorem
a.reference: Lawrence C. Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, 2nd edition, Chapter 14, 1997
a.why: The statement is the Kronecker–Weber theorem in its standard form, with the abelian field given abstractly and embedded into a cyclotomic field.

b.states: For every number field L that is abelian Galois over ℚ there are a positive natural number N and a ℚ-algebra homomorphism from L to the cyclotomic field ℚ(ζ_N). A homomorphism of fields is injective, so L embeds into a cyclotomic field.
b.known_as: the Kronecker–Weber theorem

check.known_as: the Kronecker–Weber theorem
check.note: Theorem 8 states the same theorem with the abelian field placed inside an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, where this statement embeds it into a cyclotomic field by a ℚ-algebra map.

theorems.name: UpperTheory.V.CF.kw
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, field theory

a.states: For every algebraically closed field Ω of characteristic zero and every subfield L of Ω that is finite and Galois over ℚ with abelian Galois group, there are a positive integer N and a primitive N-th root of unity ζ in Ω such that L is contained in ℚ(ζ). This is the Kronecker–Weber theorem for abelian fields given as subfields of a fixed algebraically closed field.
a.notation: ∀ algebraically closed Ω with char Ω = 0, ∀ L ⊆ Ω finite abelian over ℚ, ∃ N ≥ 1, ∃ ζ ∈ Ω primitive N-th root of unity with L ⊆ ℚ(ζ)
a.known_as: the Kronecker–Weber theorem
a.reference: Lawrence C. Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, 2nd edition, Chapter 14, 1997
a.why: The statement is the Kronecker–Weber theorem with the abelian field placed inside an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, which is only a different way of writing the standard form.

b.states: For every algebraically closed field Ω of characteristic zero and every subfield L of Ω that is finite-dimensional and abelian Galois over ℚ, there are a positive natural number N and a primitive N-th root of unity ζ in Ω such that L is contained in ℚ(ζ).
b.known_as: the Kronecker–Weber theorem

check.known_as: the Kronecker–Weber theorem
check.note: The statement is equivalent to theorem 7, because every number field embeds into an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and a field that is normal over ℚ has the same image under every embedding into that field.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.stein_factorisation_connected_fibres
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: For all schemes X and Y and every proper morphism g from X to Y with Y locally noetherian, there are a scheme Y′, a morphism a from X to Y′ and a morphism b from Y′ to Y with g = b ∘ a, such that b is finite, a is proper and surjective, the ring map a^# from O_{Y′}(V) to O_X(a^{−1}(V)) is bijective for every open set V of Y′, and every fibre a^{−1}(y) is a preconnected subset of X. The bijectivity condition says that a_*O_X = O_{Y′}, and preconnected means connected or empty.
a.notation: Y locally noetherian, g ∈ Hom(X, Y) proper ⇒ ∃ X —a→ Y′ —b→ Y with g = b∘a, b finite, a proper and surjective, O_{Y′} ≅ a_*O_X, and a^{−1}(y) preconnected for every y ∈ Y′
a.known_as: the Stein factorization theorem
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique III, première partie, §4.3, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 11, 1961
a.why: The published theorem gives the same factorization and in addition identifies Y′ as the relative spectrum of g_*O_X and shows that the fibres of a are geometrically connected, so the Lean statement claims a little less.

b.states: Let X and Y be schemes in universe 0, with Y locally Noetherian, and let g be a proper morphism from X to Y. Then there are a scheme Y', a morphism a from X to Y' and a morphism b from Y' to Y with g = b ∘ a, b finite, a proper and surjective, every section map of a from O_{Y'}(V) to O_X(a⁻¹V) bijective, and every fibre of a preconnected. The bijectivity says that O_{Y'} → a_*O_X is an isomorphism. Surjectivity makes the fibres nonempty, so they are connected.
b.known_as: the Stein factorization theorem together with Zariski's connectedness of its fibres, as in EGA III §4.3 and Hartshorne III.11.5

check.known_as: the Stein factorization theorem (EGA III 4.3.3, Hartshorne III.11.5)
check.vacuity: None found, and the surjectivity of a makes every fibre nonempty, so the preconnected fibres are connected.
check.note: The stated properties force Y′ to be the relative spectrum of g_*O_X, because b is finite and a_*O_X = O_{Y′} gives g_*O_X = b_*O_{Y′}, so the Lean text leaves out only the geometric connectedness of the fibres that EGA and the Stacks Project add, which is the gap behind reader A's verdict weaker.

theorems.name: PositivityTheory.Xgn.SpecialFibreConnected.isConnected_closed
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: Let O be a noetherian local ring, Z a scheme and f a proper morphism from Z to Spec O such that the ring map from O through Γ(Spec O) to Γ(Z, O_Z) induced by f is bijective. Then the fibre of f over the closed point of Spec O is a nonempty connected subset of Z.
a.notation: O noetherian local, f ∈ Hom(Z, Spec O) proper, O ≅ Γ(Z, O_Z) via f^# ⇒ f^{−1}(closed point) nonempty and connected
a.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem, in the case of a local base and its closed point
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique III, première partie, §4.3, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 11, 1961
a.vacuity: None found, and the nonemptiness in the conclusion is genuine content, which holds because Z is nonempty when Γ(Z, O_Z) ≅ O and the closed image of f then contains the closed point.
a.why: Zariski's theorem gives connected fibres of a proper f with f_*O_Z = O_Y over a locally noetherian Y, and over the affine base Spec O the condition on global sections is equivalent to f_*O_Z = O_Y because f_*O_Z is quasi-coherent.

b.states: Let Z be a scheme, O a Noetherian local ring and f a proper morphism from Z to Spec O, and suppose that the composite map from O to the global sections Γ(Z, O_Z) is bijective. Then the fibre of f over the closed point of Spec O is connected, and in Mathlib connectedness includes being nonempty.
b.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem, here over a Noetherian local base and for the closed fibre
b.vacuity: None found, and the nonemptiness in the conclusion follows without being assumed, since the bijectivity excludes an empty Z for a nonzero ring O and a proper map from a nonempty scheme to a local scheme reaches the closed point.

check.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem, for a noetherian local base and its closed fibre
check.vacuity: None found, and the nonemptiness in the conclusion is real content, which holds because a local ring is nonzero, so Z is nonempty and the closed image of f contains the closed point.
check.note: The hypothesis on global sections alone suffices because the base is affine and f_*O_Z is quasi-coherent, which makes the hypothesis equivalent to f_*O_Z = O_{Spec O}.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.ZariskiSections.finite_appTop_restrict
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: For a proper morphism π from a scheme Y to a locally noetherian scheme Z and an affine open subset V of Z, the ring map from Γ(V, O_Z) to Γ(π^{−1}(V), O_Y) induced by the restriction of π over V is finite. In other words, Γ(π^{−1}(V), O_Y) is a finitely generated module over Γ(V, O_Z).
a.notation: π ∈ Hom(Y, Z) proper, Z locally noetherian, V ⊆ Z affine open ⇒ Γ(π^{−1}V, O_Y) finite over Γ(V, O_Z)
a.known_as: the finiteness of sections under a proper morphism, the degree zero case of Grothendieck's coherence theorem for direct images under proper morphisms
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique III, première partie, §3.2, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 11, 1961
a.why: The coherence theorem says that π_*O_Y is a coherent O_Z-module, and the Lean statement is the value of that sheaf on one affine open set.

b.states: Let π be a proper morphism from Y to Z with Z locally Noetherian, and let V be an affine open of Z. Then the ring map from Γ(V, O_Z) to Γ(π⁻¹V, O_Y) that the restriction of π over V induces is finite, which means that Γ(π⁻¹V, O_Y) is a finitely generated module over Γ(V, O_Z). Put another way, π_*O_Y is a coherent O_Z-module.
b.known_as: the coherence of π_*O_Y for a proper morphism π, the degree-zero case for the structure sheaf of Grothendieck's finiteness theorem for proper morphisms (EGA III 3.2.1)

check.known_as: the coherence of π_*O_Y for a proper morphism π to a locally noetherian scheme, the degree-zero case for the structure sheaf of Grothendieck's finiteness theorem for proper morphisms (EGA III 3.2.1)
check.note: Theorem 12 proves the same finiteness under the weaker hypothesis that only the ring of sections over the affine open set is noetherian.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.SteinFact.finite_app_of_isProper
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: For a proper morphism g from a scheme X to a scheme Y and an affine open subset V of Y whose ring of sections Γ(V, O_Y) is noetherian, the ring map g^# from Γ(V, O_Y) to Γ(g^{−1}(V), O_X) is finite. Unlike theorem 11, it asks only that this one ring be noetherian and not that the whole of Y be locally noetherian.
a.notation: g ∈ Hom(X, Y) proper, V ⊆ Y affine open with Γ(V, O_Y) noetherian ⇒ Γ(g^{−1}V, O_X) finite over Γ(V, O_Y)
a.known_as: the finiteness of sections under a proper morphism, the degree zero case of Grothendieck's coherence theorem for direct images under proper morphisms
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique III, première partie, §3.2, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 11, 1961
a.why: Restricting g over V gives a proper morphism to the noetherian affine scheme V, and the coherence theorem applied to that morphism gives the statement directly.

b.states: For every proper morphism g from X to Y and every affine open V of Y whose ring of sections Γ(Y, V) is Noetherian, the section map from Γ(Y, V) to Γ(X, g⁻¹V) is finite. Only the ring over the affine open V has to be Noetherian, and Y as a whole need not be locally Noetherian.
b.known_as: the coherence of g_*O_X for a proper morphism g, the degree-zero case for the structure sheaf of Grothendieck's finiteness theorem for proper morphisms (EGA III 3.2.1)

check.known_as: the coherence of g_*O_X for a proper morphism g, the degree-zero case for the structure sheaf of Grothendieck's finiteness theorem for proper morphisms (EGA III 3.2.1)
check.note: The weaker noetherian hypothesis suffices because the restriction of g over V is a proper morphism to the noetherian affine scheme V, to which the finiteness theorem applies.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.ProfCoh.exists_zmod_char_not_norm
theorems.areas: other number theory, topology, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with separable closure Ω, and let n be a natural number whose image in F is nonzero. If an element a of F^× is not the n-th power of any element of F^×, then there is a group homomorphism ψ from Gal(Ω/F) to ℤ/nℤ with open kernel such that a is not the norm of any element of the fixed field L of the kernel of ψ. The field L is a cyclic extension of F of degree dividing n, so the conclusion says that a lies outside the norm group N_{L/F}(L^×).
a.notation: F nonarchimedean local, n·1_F ≠ 0, a ∈ F^× ∖ (F^×)^n ⇒ ∃ ψ ∈ Hom(Gal(F^sep/F), ℤ/n) with open kernel and a ∉ N_{L/F}(L) for L = (F^sep)^{ker ψ}
a.known_as: the consequence of local class field theory that (F^×)^n is the intersection of the norm groups of the cyclic extensions of F of degree dividing n, which is the nondegeneracy of the local duality pairing between H^1(F, ℤ/n) and F^×/(F^×)^n
a.reference: Jürgen Neukirch, Alexander Schmidt and Kay Wingberg, Cohomology of Number Fields, 2nd edition, 2008
a.vacuity: None found, since F = ℚ_p with n = 2 and a = p meets every hypothesis, and ψ is forced to be nontrivial because a is a norm from F itself.
a.why: The statement follows at once from the reciprocity and existence theorems of local class field theory, but it is phrased with Galois characters in the way a proof of local Tate duality needs, so it could also count as a technical step.

b.states: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with separable closure Ω, let n be a natural number that is nonzero in F, and let a be a unit of F that is not the n-th power of any unit. Then there is a group homomorphism ψ from Gal(Ω/F) to ℤ/nℤ with open kernel such that a is not the norm to F of any element of the fixed field of the kernel of ψ. That fixed field is a finite cyclic extension of F whose degree divides n.
b.known_as: the nondegeneracy of the norm residue pairing of local class field theory, in the form that an element which is a norm from every cyclic extension of degree dividing n is an n-th power, which is one half of local Tate duality between H^1(F, ℤ/n) and F^×/F^{×n}
b.vacuity: The hypotheses cannot be met for n = 0 or n = 1, but for every n ≥ 2 that is nonzero in F a uniformizer of F meets them, so the statement is not empty.

check.known_as: the half of the nondegeneracy of the local duality pairing between H^1(F, ℤ/nℤ) and F^×/(F^×)^n which says that an element of F^× that is a norm from every cyclic extension of degree dividing n is an n-th power, a consequence of local class field theory
check.vacuity: None found, since a uniformizer of F meets the hypotheses for every n ≥ 2 that is nonzero in F, while the hypotheses themselves exclude n = 0 and n = 1.
check.note: The field F may have positive characteristic, and the hypothesis that n is nonzero in F is what makes (F^×)^n an open subgroup of finite index, so that the existence theorem of local class field theory applies to it.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.LocalField.Padic.exists_le_adjoin_rootsOfUnity
theorems.areas: p-adic numbers, linear algebra, field theory

a.states: Let p be a prime and Ω a separable closure of the field ℚ_p of p-adic numbers. For every intermediate field L between ℚ_p and Ω that is finite over ℚ_p and Galois with abelian Galois group, there is a positive integer N such that L is contained in the field generated over ℚ_p by all N-th roots of unity in Ω.
a.notation: ∀ prime p, ∀ finite abelian L/ℚ_p inside a separable closure Ω, ∃ N ≥ 1 with L ⊆ ℚ_p(μ_N)
a.known_as: the local Kronecker–Weber theorem
a.reference: Lawrence C. Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, 2nd edition, Chapter 14, 1997
a.why: The statement is the local Kronecker–Weber theorem over ℚ_p with the abelian extension placed inside a fixed separable closure.

b.states: Let p be a prime and Ω a separably closed field that is separable algebraic over ℚ_p, which makes Ω an algebraic closure of ℚ_p. For every intermediate field L of Ω over ℚ_p that is finite and abelian Galois over ℚ_p there is a positive natural number N such that L is contained in the field generated over ℚ_p by the N-th roots of unity in Ω.
b.known_as: the local Kronecker–Weber theorem for ℚ_p

check.known_as: the local Kronecker–Weber theorem for ℚ_p
check.note: The instances IsSepClosed and Algebra.IsSeparable make Ω a separable closure of ℚ_p, which is an algebraic closure because ℚ_p has characteristic zero.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.pic_localization_strictHenselisation_no_torsion
theorems.areas: ring theory, field theory, group theory

a.states: Let T be a local domain in which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root, and let q be a positive integer that is a unit in T. Let O be a henselian local ring with separably closed residue field that is an algebra over T[X], compatibly with T, and is the directed union of T[X]-subalgebras each isomorphic to the localization of an étale T[X]-algebra at a prime ideal, a condition that a strict henselization of T[X] satisfies. Then the Picard group of the localization of O at the nonzero elements of T, which is O ⊗_T K for the fraction field K of T, has no nontrivial element whose q-th power is trivial.
a.notation: T absolutely integrally closed local domain, q ∈ T^×, O strictly henselian and a directed union of local rings of étale T[X]-algebras ⇒ Pic(O ⊗_T Frac T)[q] = 0
a.known_as: no published result known, a technical lemma saying that the Picard group of the generic fibre of a strict henselization of the affine line over an absolutely integrally closed local domain has no q-torsion, of the kind used in proofs of the local acyclicity of smooth morphisms
a.vacuity: None found, since an algebraically closed field T with O the strict henselization of T[X] at the origin meets every hypothesis, although in that case the localization equals the local ring O and the conclusion is immediate, so the content lies in the case of a non-field T such as a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field.
a.why: The hypotheses are tailored to one step of a larger argument, and although the statement resembles lemmas in proofs of the smooth base change theorem, I know no published lemma in this exact form.

b.states: Let T be a local domain in which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root, which makes T integrally closed with an algebraically closed fraction field K. Let O be a henselian local ring with separably closed residue field that is a compatible algebra over T and over T[X], and that is the directed union of T[X]-subalgebras each isomorphic over T[X] to the local ring of an étale T[X]-algebra at a prime ideal. This is the shape of a strict henselization of T[X] at a prime ideal. Then for every positive natural number q that is a unit in T, the only element of the Picard group of the localization of O at the nonzero elements of T (that is, O ⊗_T K) whose q-th power is trivial is the identity.
b.known_as: no published result known
b.vacuity: None found, since T = ℂ with O the henselization of ℂ[X] at (X) meets every hypothesis, although for a field T the localization is O itself and the conclusion holds at once because a local ring has trivial Picard group.

check.known_as: no published result known, a lemma that the Picard group of the generic fibre over T of a strictly henselian local ring of the affine line over an absolutely integrally closed local domain T has no q-torsion
check.vacuity: None found, since a valuation ring with algebraically closed fraction field gives a case with content, although for a field T the localization is the local ring O itself and the conclusion holds at once because a local ring has trivial Picard group.
check.note: The ring whose Picard group is studied inverts only the nonzero elements of T, so it is in general not local, and the hypotheses describe the strict henselization of T[X] at a prime by its shape as a directed union without naming it.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.isProper_of_properSpecialFibre_universallyOpen_dvr
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics

a.states: Let W be a discrete valuation ring with residue field k, and let f be a morphism from a scheme X to Spec W that is separated, locally of finite type, quasi-compact and universally open, and whose fibres are geometrically irreducible. If the special fibre X ×_{Spec W} Spec k is proper over k, then f is proper.
a.notation: W DVR, f ∈ Hom(X, Spec W) separated, of finite type, universally open, with geometrically irreducible fibres, X_k proper over k ⇒ f proper
a.known_as: a properness criterion through the special fibre, which I relate to Grothendieck's results on the set of proper fibres of a separated universally open morphism of finite type with geometrically connected fibres
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique IV, troisième partie, §15.7, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 28, 1966
a.vacuity: None found, since the projective line over W meets every hypothesis, and Mathlib's geometric irreducibility forces every fibre to be nonempty, which rules out the degenerate example of the generic point Spec K mapping to Spec W.
a.why: I am confident that the statement is true, because universal openness makes the generic fibre dense in X and Zariski's connectedness theorem then forces a compactification of X to coincide with X, but I am not sure of the exact form of the published criterion that it specializes.

b.states: Let W be a discrete valuation ring and f a morphism from a scheme X to Spec W that is separated, locally of finite type, quasi-compact, universally open and geometrically irreducible. Under Mathlib's convention this last condition makes every fibre irreducible and hence nonempty. If the base change of f to the residue field of W, which is the special fibre, is proper, then f is proper.
b.known_as: a properness criterion over a discrete valuation ring by a proper special fibre for separated finite-type universally open morphisms with geometrically connected fibres, which I recall from EGA IV_3 §15.7 without certainty about its exact form

check.known_as: a properness criterion through the special fibre over a discrete valuation ring, the case of Spec W of Grothendieck's theorem that the points with proper fibre form an open and closed set for a separated universally open morphism of finite type with geometrically connected fibres (EGA IV_3 15.7.10)
check.vacuity: None found, since the projective line over W meets every hypothesis, and the nonemptiness of fibres that Mathlib builds into geometric irreducibility excludes the open immersion of the generic point into Spec W, which would otherwise be a counterexample.
check.note: Neither reader is sure of the exact published form, so the reference to EGA IV_3 15.7.10 should be checked against the text before it is cited.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.zariski_connectedness_isPreconnected_fibre
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: For all schemes X and Y and every proper morphism a from X to Y with Y locally noetherian such that the ring map a^# from O_Y(V) to O_X(a^{−1}(V)) is bijective for every open set V of Y, every fibre a^{−1}(y) is a preconnected subset of X. The bijectivity condition says that a_*O_X = O_Y, and preconnected means connected or empty.
a.notation: Y locally noetherian, a ∈ Hom(X, Y) proper, O_Y ≅ a_*O_X ⇒ a^{−1}(y) preconnected for every y ∈ Y
a.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique III, première partie, §4.3, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 11, 1961
a.vacuity: None found, and the hypotheses even force a to be surjective, so every fibre is nonempty and connected.
a.why: The hypotheses and the conclusion are those of Zariski's connectedness theorem for proper morphisms to a locally noetherian base, and the gap between preconnected and connected closes because the fibres are nonempty.

b.states: Let X and Y be schemes in universe 0, with Y locally Noetherian, and let a be a proper morphism from X to Y. Suppose that every section map of a from O_Y(V) to O_X(a⁻¹V) is bijective, which says that O_Y → a_*O_X is an isomorphism. Then every fibre of a is preconnected. Preconnectedness allows an empty fibre, although the hypotheses already force a to be surjective.
b.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem (EGA III 4.3.1, Hartshorne III.11.3)

check.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem (EGA III 4.3.1, Hartshorne III.11.3)
check.vacuity: None found, and the hypotheses force a to be surjective, so every fibre is nonempty and the preconnected fibres are connected.
check.note: The bijectivity of the section maps over every open set V of Y is the usual hypothesis a_*O_X = O_Y, and the conclusion gives connected fibres as in EGA III 4.3.1 and leaves out their geometric connectedness.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.isProper_of_irreducible_properSpecialFibre_completeDvr
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k, and let f be a separated and quasi-compact morphism locally of finite type from an irreducible scheme X to Spec O. If some point of X maps to the closed point of Spec O and the special fibre X ×_{Spec O} Spec k is proper over k, then f is proper.
a.notation: O complete DVR, X irreducible, f ∈ Hom(X, Spec O) separated of finite type, X_k ≠ ∅ proper over k ⇒ f proper
a.known_as: a special case of the decomposition lemma for a separated scheme of finite type over a henselian local ring, which splits off an open and closed part that is proper over the base and has a given open and closed proper part of the special fibre
a.reference: The Stacks Project Authors, The Stacks Project, chapter More on Morphisms, 2024
a.vacuity: None found, and the completeness of O is needed, because over a non-henselian discrete valuation ring the spectrum of a finite semilocal Dedekind extension with two maximal ideals, with one of them removed, meets the other hypotheses but is not proper.
a.why: The statement is true by Nagata compactification, Stein factorization over a henselian base and Zariski's connectedness theorem, but I recall the general henselian lemma without its exact location, so the named source is uncertain.

b.states: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring and f a separated, locally finite-type and quasi-compact morphism from an irreducible scheme X to Spec O, with some point of X mapping to the closed point. If the special fibre of f, which is its base change to the residue field, is proper, then f is proper.
b.known_as: no published result known

check.known_as: a special case of the lemma that a separated scheme of finite type over a henselian local ring has an open and closed subscheme that is proper over the base and whose special fibre is any prescribed open and closed part of the special fibre that is proper (Stacks Project, More on Morphisms)
check.vacuity: None found, since the projective line over O meets every hypothesis.
check.note: The completeness of O is used only through the henselian property, and it cannot simply be dropped, since over a non-henselian discrete valuation ring an open part of the spectrum of a finite semilocal Dedekind extension meets the other hypotheses and is not proper.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.isClosed_image_closure_completeDVR_specialFibre
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k, let s be a proper morphism from a scheme P to Spec O and q an immersion from a scheme Y into P, and assume that the special fibre of the composite morphism from Y to Spec O is proper over k. For every irreducible subset C of Y whose closure in Y contains a point lying over the closed point of Spec O, the image under q of the closure of C is closed in P.
a.notation: O complete DVR, s ∈ Hom(P, Spec O) proper, q ∈ Hom(Y, P) immersion, Y_k proper over k, C ⊆ Y irreducible with cl(C) ∩ Y_k ≠ ∅ ⇒ q(cl C) closed in P
a.known_as: no published result known, a closedness lemma for a locally closed subscheme with proper special fibre inside a proper scheme over a complete discrete valuation ring, which follows from the properness criterion of theorem 18 applied to the closure of C
a.vacuity: None found, since an irreducible P proper over O with Y = P and C = P meets every hypothesis.
a.why: The statement is shaped for one use, with an immersion and an irreducible set as inputs, and I know it only as a direct corollary of the properness criterion and not as a published lemma.

b.states: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring, s a proper morphism from P to Spec O, and q an immersion from Y to P such that the special fibre of the composite of q and s is proper. Then for every irreducible subset C of Y whose closure contains a point mapping to the closed point of Spec O, the image under q of the closure of C is closed in P.
b.known_as: no published result known

check.known_as: no published result known, a closedness lemma for an immersed scheme with proper special fibre inside a proper scheme over a complete discrete valuation ring
check.vacuity: None found, since an irreducible scheme P proper over O with Y = P and C = P meets every hypothesis.
check.note: The statement follows from theorem 18 applied to the closure of C with its reduced structure, which is irreducible, separated and of finite type over O with a nonempty special fibre that is proper because it is closed in the special fibre of Y.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.zariskiConnectedness_isPreconnected_fibre_affine
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: Let X be an affine locally noetherian scheme and f a proper morphism from a scheme Y to X such that the ring map f^# from Γ(X, O_X) to Γ(Y, O_Y) is bijective. Then every fibre f^{−1}(x) is a preconnected subset of Y, which means connected or empty.
a.notation: X affine noetherian, f ∈ Hom(Y, X) proper, Γ(X, O_X) ≅ Γ(Y, O_Y) via f^# ⇒ f^{−1}(x) preconnected for every x ∈ X
a.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem, in the case of an affine base
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique III, première partie, §4.3, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 11, 1961
a.why: Over an affine base the sheaf f_*O_Y is quasi-coherent, so bijectivity on global sections is the same as O_X = f_*O_Y, and the statement is Zariski's theorem restricted to affine bases.

b.states: Let f be a proper morphism from Y to an affine, locally Noetherian scheme X, and suppose that the map on global sections from Γ(X, O_X) to Γ(Y, O_Y) is bijective. Then the fibre of f over every point x of X is preconnected. Over an affine base this hypothesis on global sections is the same as O_X → f_*O_Y being an isomorphism, because f_*O_Y is quasi-coherent.
b.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem for an affine Noetherian base

check.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem, over an affine noetherian base
check.vacuity: None found, and the hypotheses force f to be surjective, so every fibre is nonempty.
check.note: Over the affine base the condition on global sections is equivalent to f_*O_Y = O_X because f_*O_Y is quasi-coherent, and theorem 17 is the same theorem over any locally noetherian base.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.ZariskiConn.isPreconnected_closedFibre
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: Let O be a Noetherian local ring that is complete and separated for the adic topology of its maximal ideal, and let f from a scheme Y to Spec O be a proper morphism. If the underlying space of Y is preconnected, then the preimage under f of the closed point of Spec O is preconnected. Since preconnected allows the empty set, the statement says that a connected scheme proper over O has a connected closed fibre.
a.notation: (O, 𝔪) Noetherian local and 𝔪-adically complete, f: Y → Spec O proper, Y preconnected ⟹ f⁻¹({𝔪}) preconnected
a.known_as: Zariski's connectedness theorem in its form over a complete Noetherian local base, by which the connected components of a scheme proper over such a ring correspond to those of its closed fibre
a.reference: A. Grothendieck and J. Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique III. Étude cohomologique des faisceaux cohérents, première partie, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 11, 1961
a.why: The statement follows from the theorem on formal functions and the Stein factorization in the cited work, but I cannot point to the exact place where it is stated in this one-directional form.

b.states: Let O be a Noetherian local ring that is complete and separated for the topology of its maximal ideal, let Y be a scheme with a proper morphism f to Spec O, and let Y be preconnected. Then the preimage under f of the closed point of Spec O, the closed fibre, is a preconnected subset of Y.
b.known_as: Connectedness of the closed fibre of a proper scheme with connected source over a complete Noetherian local ring, the consequence of Grothendieck's theorem on formal functions that underlies Zariski's connectedness theorem (EGA III 4.3, Hartshorne III.11)

check.known_as: the local form of Zariski's connectedness theorem, by which a connected scheme proper over a complete Noetherian local ring has a connected closed fibre, a corollary of the theorem on formal functions and the Stein factorisation (EGA III 4.3)
check.note: The Lean text gives only the direction from a preconnected Y to a preconnected closed fibre, and since preconnected allows the empty set, the nonemptiness of the closed fibre of a nonempty Y that A's gloss uses comes from properness and not from the stated conclusion.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.gaussian_fourier_self_dual_adelic
theorems.areas: number fields, measure theory, complex analysis, special functions, other analysis, topology, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let F be a totally real number field of degree d, B a nonsingular symmetric matrix over F of size 2M with M ≥ 3, Q(x) = ½ xᵀBx, and P_w a positive definite majorant of B at each real place w, meaning P_w B_w⁻¹ P_w = B_w. Fix a Haar measure on the finite adeles A_f that gives the integral adeles mass 1 and a probability space carrying measurable elements g_∞,w(ω) of the real orthogonal groups of B and g_f(ω) of O(B)(A_f), and assume that for each N ≥ 1 the expected number of nonzero x ∈ F^{2M} with N g_f(ω)x integral and every ‖g_∞,w(ω)x‖ ≤ R is at most C_N(R^{dM} + R^{2dM}) for all R > 0. Then there are a constant C, continuous nonnegative densities D_f(a, ·) on A_f of the image under Q of Haar measure on {x | a x integral}, and a continuous nonnegative density D_∞ on ℝ^{places} of the image under (Q_w)_w of the Gaussian exp(−π Σ_w x_wᵀ P_w x_w) dx. For every integer a ≥ 1 the expectation I of the sum of exp(−π Σ_w (g_∞,w(ω)x)ᵀ P_w g_∞,w(ω)x) over nonzero x ∈ F^{2M} with Q(x) = 0 and a g_f(ω)x integral is finite and satisfies |I − |Δ_F|^{−(2M−1)/2} D_f(a, 0) D_∞(0)| ≤ C a^{dM}, where Δ_F is the discriminant of F.
a.notation: E_ω Σ_{x ∈ F^{2M}∖{0}, Q(x) = 0, a g_f(ω)x ∈ Ô^{2M}} exp(−π Σ_w ‖g_∞,w(ω)x‖²_{P_w}) = I(a) with |I(a) − |Δ_F|^{−(2M−1)/2} D_f(a, 0) D_∞(0)| ≤ C a^{dM} for all a ≥ 1
a.known_as: no published result known, a quantitative Siegel–Weil type asymptotic with error of order a^{dM} for the averaged Gaussian-weighted count of nonzero isotropic vectors of a quadratic form in 2M ≥ 6 variables over a totally real field
a.why: The probability-space framing with an assumed averaged counting bound is tailored to the project, and although the main term is the product of local densities from Siegel's formula I know no published estimate in this form.

b.states: Take a totally real number field F of degree d, a symmetric matrix B over F of size 2M with M ≥ 3 and nonzero determinant, the real embeddings ρ_w of the infinite places, positive definite real matrices P_w with P_w B_w⁻¹ P_w = B_w, a Haar measure on the finite adeles that gives the integral adeles volume 1, and a probability space Ω with measurable maps ω ↦ g_w(ω) into the real orthogonal groups of the B_w and ω ↦ g_f(ω) into the orthogonal group of B over the finite adeles. Assume that for every N > 0 there is C such that for every R > 0 the expected number of nonzero x in F^{2M} with N·g_f(ω)x integral at every finite place and with sup norm of g_w(ω)x at most R at every infinite place is at most C(R^{dM} + R^{2dM}). Then there are a constant C, continuous nonnegative functions Df(a, ·) on the finite adeles that are the densities of the image of the product Haar measure on {x | a·x integral} under Q(x) = ½xᵀBx, and a continuous nonnegative density Dinf of the image of exp(−π Σ_w x_wᵀP_w x_w)dx under x ↦ (Q_w(x_w))_w. For every positive integer a the expected value of the sum of exp(−π Σ_w (g_w x)ᵀP_w(g_w x)) over the nonzero x in F^{2M} with Q(x) = 0 and a·g_f x integral is a finite number I with |I − |disc F|^{−(2M−1)/2}·Df(a, 0)·Dinf(0)| ≤ C·a^{dM}.
b.known_as: A Siegel–Weil (Siegel mass formula) type comparison of an averaged Gaussian theta sum over isotropic vectors with the product of the singular series and the singular integral at 0, in the spirit of the Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic for the zeros of a quadratic form in at least five variables
b.vacuity: None found, and because Ω may be a one-point space, for which the counting hypothesis holds automatically, the claim contains a pointwise estimate for every single choice of orthogonal elements.

check.known_as: no published result known, a quantitative Siegel mass formula or Hardy–Littlewood type asymptotic with error of order a^{dM} for the averaged Gaussian-weighted count of nonzero isotropic vectors of a nondegenerate quadratic form in 2M ≥ 6 variables over a totally real field
check.vacuity: None found, since a one-point probability space with any single choice of orthogonal elements meets the averaged counting hypothesis.
check.note: By scaling, Df(a, 0) equals a^{2d(M−1)} times Df(1, 0) with d the degree of F, so against the error C·a^{dM} the estimate is a genuine asymptotic exactly because M ≥ 3, and the constant C is uniform in a but may depend on all other data, Ω included.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.ProfCoh.eq_top_of_forall_exists_norm
theorems.areas: other number theory, topology, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with separable closure Ω and Galois group G = Gal(Ω/F), and let H be an open normal subgroup of G that contains every commutator στσ⁻¹τ⁻¹. These conditions make the fixed field L of H a finite abelian extension of F. If every element of F^× is the norm from L to F of an element of L, then H = G, which means L = F.
a.notation: H ⊴ Gal(Ω/F) open, [G, G] ⊆ H, F^× ⊆ N_{Ω^H/F}(Ω^H) ⟹ H = Gal(Ω/F)
a.known_as: the norm index equality of local class field theory, by which the index of N_{L/F}(L^×) in F^× equals the degree of L over F for a finite abelian extension L/F
a.reference: J.-P. Serre, Local Fields, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 67, 1979
a.why: A nontrivial abelian L would by the norm index equality have a norm group of index greater than one, so the Lean statement is the immediate corollary that a norm group equal to F^× forces L = F.

b.states: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field with separable closure Ω, and let H be an open normal subgroup of Gal(Ω/F) that contains every commutator, so that its fixed field E is a finite abelian extension of F. If every element of F^× is the norm of some element of E, then H is the whole Galois group, which means E = F.
b.known_as: The corollary of the norm index equality of local class field theory, which says that for a finite abelian extension E of F the index of the norm group N(E^×) in F^× equals the degree of E over F
b.vacuity: None found, and the normality of H already follows from the commutator condition.

check.known_as: the corollary of the norm index equality of local class field theory, by which the index of N_{L/F}(L^×) in F^× equals the degree of L over F for a finite abelian extension L/F, that a finite abelian extension whose norm group is all of F^× is trivial
check.note: The normality hypothesis on H is implied by the commutator condition, and the openness of H makes the fixed field finite over F, so the norm in the hypothesis is the field norm of a finite extension.
