theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.classNumber_finite_integralLevel_closedSubgroupGL
theorems.areas: number fields, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let F be a number field and S a set of polynomials over F in the n² entries of an n × n matrix such that, for every commutative F-algebra B, the invertible matrices over B that satisfy all of S contain the identity and are closed under products and inverses. This makes S the set of equations of a linear algebraic group G ⊆ GL_n over F. Then there is a finite set T ⊆ G(A_f), with A_f the finite adeles of F, such that every x ∈ G(A_f) equals γ s u with γ ∈ G(F), s ∈ T and u ∈ G(A_f) such that u and u⁻¹ have entries integral at every finite place.
a.notation: G = V(S) ∩ GL_n a subgroup scheme over F ⟹ G(F) \ G(A_f) / (G(A_f) ∩ GL_n(Ô_F)) is finite
a.known_as: Borel's finiteness of class numbers for linear algebraic groups over number fields
a.reference: A. Borel, Some finiteness properties of adele groups over number fields, Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS 16, 1963
a.why: The Lean statement is Borel's theorem for the particular compact open subgroup of points with integral entries and integral inverse, with the group given by its defining equations inside GL_n.

b.states: Let F be a number field and S a set of polynomials over F in the n² matrix entries whose common zeros in GL_n(B) contain the identity and are closed under products and inverses for every commutative F-algebra B, so that S defines a closed subgroup scheme G of GL_n. Then there is a finite set T of points of G over the finite adeles such that every point x of G over the finite adeles can be written x = γ·s·u with γ a point of G over F embedded diagonally, s in T, and u a point of G over the finite adeles whose entries and whose inverse's entries are integral at every finite place.
b.known_as: Finiteness of the class number of a linear algebraic group over a number field (Borel 1963, Platonov–Rapinchuk Theorem 5.1), here for the open compact subgroup of finite adelic points with integral entries

check.known_as: Borel's finiteness of the class number of a linear algebraic group over a number field (Borel 1963, Platonov–Rapinchuk Theorem 5.1), with the class number taken for the integral structure that the embedding in GL_n gives
check.note: Platonov and Rapinchuk define the class number with exactly this subgroup of points with integral entries and integral inverse, and because any two compact open subgroups of G(A_f) are commensurable, finiteness here also gives finiteness for every compact open subgroup, which is why A's special case and B's same describe one content.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.LocAcycUnits.units_localization_pow_surj
theorems.areas: ring theory, field theory, group theory

a.states: Let T be a local domain in which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root, a condition that makes T integrally closed with algebraically closed fraction field K. Let O be a Henselian local ring with separably closed residue field that is an algebra over T and over T[X] compatibly, and assume O is the union of a directed family of T[X]-subalgebras each isomorphic over T[X] to the localization of an étale T[X]-algebra at a prime ideal. Let q be a positive integer that is a unit in T. Then every unit of O ⊗_T K, the localization of O at the images of the nonzero elements of T, is the q-th power of a unit.
a.notation: T absolutely integrally closed local domain, O strictly Henselian and ind-étale over T[X], q ∈ T^× ⟹ ∀ u ∈ (O ⊗_T K)^× ∃ v ∈ (O ⊗_T K)^× with v^q = u
a.known_as: the vanishing of H¹ with coefficients μ_q on the geometric generic fibre of a strict henselization of the affine line, from the proof that smooth morphisms are locally acyclic, in its unit part through the Kummer sequence
a.reference: M. Artin, Morphismes acycliques, Exposé XV in Théorie des topos et cohomologie étale des schémas (SGA 4), tome 3, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 305, 1973
a.why: The Kummer sequence turns the published vanishing of H¹ into the q-divisibility of units, but the Lean hypotheses describe the strict henselization only indirectly, so the match with the published setting rests on routine identifications.

b.states: Let T be a local domain over which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root, let q be a positive integer that is a unit in T, and let O be a henselian local T[X]-algebra with separably closed residue field that is a directed union of subalgebras, each isomorphic over T[X] to the localization at a prime of an étale T[X]-algebra. Then every unit of the localization of O at the images of the nonzero elements of T is the q-th power of a unit of that localization.
b.known_as: The step in the proof that smooth morphisms are locally acyclic (SGA 4 XV, Deligne's Arcata in SGA 4½) which shows that the units of the generic fibre of a strict localization of the affine line over an absolutely integrally closed strictly local base are q-th powers for q invertible, so that the Kummer part of H¹ vanishes
b.vacuity: None found, and the repeated assumption that T is a domain is redundant.

check.known_as: the q-divisibility of the units of the generic fibre of a strict henselization of the affine line over an absolutely integrally closed strictly local base, the unit part, through the Kummer sequence, of the vanishing of H¹ with μ_q coefficients in Artin's proof that smooth morphisms are locally acyclic (SGA 4 XV, Deligne's Arcata in SGA 4½)
check.note: A local domain in which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root is strictly henselian with algebraically closed fraction field, so the Lean base matches the published one, while O is described only through its properties and may lie over any prime of T[X], and the repeated IsDomain T and the condition 0 < q add nothing.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.units_localization_strictHenselian_eq_const_mul_unit
theorems.areas: ring theory, field theory, group theory

a.states: Let T be a local domain in which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root, a condition that makes T integrally closed with algebraically closed fraction field K. Let O be a Henselian local ring with separably closed residue field that is an algebra over T and over T[X] compatibly, and assume O is the union of a directed family of T[X]-subalgebras each isomorphic over T[X] to the localization of an étale T[X]-algebra at a prime ideal. Then for every unit u of O ⊗_T K, the localization of O at the images of the nonzero elements of T, there are nonzero c, d ∈ T and a unit w of O with u d = c w in O ⊗_T K. Every such unit is therefore an element c/d of K^× times a unit of O.
a.notation: ∀ u ∈ (O ⊗_T K)^× ∃ c, d ∈ T∖{0}, w ∈ O^× with u d = c w, so (O ⊗_T K)^× ⊆ K^× · O^×
a.known_as: the description of the units of the geometric generic fibre of a strict henselization of the affine line as constants times units, a lemma in Artin's proof that smooth morphisms are locally acyclic
a.reference: M. Artin, Morphismes acycliques, Exposé XV in Théorie des topos et cohomologie étale des schémas (SGA 4), tome 3, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 305, 1973
a.why: I recall that a description of units of this kind enters the computation of H¹ in the proof of local acyclicity, but I cannot confirm the exact published formulation or its hypotheses.

b.states: Let T be a local domain over which every monic polynomial of positive degree has a root, and let O be a henselian local T[X]-algebra with separably closed residue field that is a directed union of subalgebras, each isomorphic over T[X] to the localization at a prime of an étale T[X]-algebra. Then for every unit u of the localization of O at the images of the nonzero elements of T there are nonzero c and d in T and a unit w of O with u·d = c·w. In other words, the units of that localization are the nonzero fractions of T times the units of O.
b.known_as: The lemma in the proof that smooth morphisms are locally acyclic (SGA 4 XV, Deligne's Arcata in SGA 4½) that the units of the generic fibre of a strict localization of the affine line over an absolutely integrally closed strictly local base are the nonzero constants times the units of the strict localization

check.known_as: the lemma in Artin's proof that smooth morphisms are locally acyclic (SGA 4 XV, Deligne's Arcata in SGA 4½) that every unit of the generic fibre of a strict henselization of the affine line over an absolutely integrally closed strictly local base is a nonzero constant times a unit of the strict henselization
check.note: The q-divisibility of number 27 follows from this decomposition, because nonzero constants of the algebraically closed fraction field and units of the henselian ring O with separably closed residue field are both q-th powers when q is invertible in T.

theorems.name: UpperTheory.Cb.exists_finite_etale_representing_clopen_subschemes
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, topology, homological algebra, combinatorics, geometry

a.states: Let S be a locally Noetherian scheme and G a finite étale S-scheme. Then there are a finite étale S-scheme Y and an open and closed subset U of Y ×_S G with a universal property. For every S-scheme T and every open and closed subset V of T ×_S G there is exactly one S-morphism y from T to Y with (y × id_G)⁻¹(U) = V. Thus Y represents the functor that sends T to the set of open and closed subsets of T ×_S G.
a.notation: ∃ Y finite étale over S, U ⊆ Y ×_S G clopen, with Hom_S(T, Y) ≅ {V ⊆ T ×_S G clopen} via y ↦ (y × id_G)⁻¹(U) for every S-scheme T
a.known_as: representability of the Weil restriction along G → S of the constant scheme S ⊔ S, which classifies open and closed subschemes of the products T ×_S G
a.reference: S. Bosch, W. Lütkebohmert and M. Raynaud, Néron Models, Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete 21, 1990
a.why: Representability and étaleness of the Weil restriction are in the cited book, while the finiteness of Y and the translation from open and closed subsets to morphisms into S ⊔ S are routine additions that I cannot tie to one published statement.

b.states: For a locally Noetherian scheme S and a finite étale S-scheme G, there are a finite étale S-scheme Y and an open subset U of Y ×_S G that is also closed, such that for every S-scheme T and every open and closed subset V of T ×_S G there is exactly one S-morphism y from T to Y with (y × id_G)⁻¹(U) = V. In other words, Y represents the functor that sends T to the open and closed subschemes of T ×_S G.
b.known_as: Representability of the functor of open and closed subschemes of the base changes of a finite étale cover by a finite étale scheme, namely the Weil restriction along G of the constant two-point scheme, or equivalently the Hilbert scheme of G over S

check.known_as: representability of the Weil restriction along a finite étale G → S of the constant scheme S ⊔ S by a finite étale S-scheme, equivalently the finite étale scheme that classifies open and closed subschemes of the base changes of G (Bosch, Lütkebohmert and Raynaud, Néron Models, Section 7.6)
check.note: The hypothesis that S is locally Noetherian is more than the published result needs, and under Galois theory Y corresponds to the set of subsets of a geometric fibre of G.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.kummer_cocycle_norm_criterion
theorems.areas: topology, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let K be a field with separable closure Ω and Galois group G, let N ≥ 1, let ζ ∈ Ω be a primitive N-th root of unity, and let c₀ be the cyclotomic character, a map from G to Z/N with g(ζ) = ζ^{c₀(g)}. Let ψ be a homomorphism from G to Z/N with open kernel, and let U ∈ K^× be a norm from the fixed field of ker ψ. If T ∈ Ω satisfies T^N = U and κ from G to Z/N satisfies g(T) = ζ^{κ(g)} T, then there is a locally constant c from G to Z/N with c₀(g) c(h) − c(gh) + c(g) = κ(g) ψ(h) for all g, h ∈ G. The left side is the coboundary of c in Z/N(1) and the right side is the cup product of the Kummer cocycle of U with ψ, so the class (U) ∪ ψ vanishes in H²(G, μ_N).
a.notation: U ∈ N_{L_ψ/K}(L_ψ^×) ⟹ ∃ c ∈ C⁰(G, Z/N(1)) with c₀(g)c(h) − c(gh) + c(g) = κ_U(g)ψ(h), that is κ_U ∪ ψ = dc
a.known_as: the norm criterion for the splitting of a cyclic algebra, in the direction that a norm b from L_χ gives (χ, b) = 0, written with the Kummer class of b in H²(K, μ_N)
a.reference: P. Gille and T. Szamuely, Central Simple Algebras and Galois Cohomology, Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics 101, 2006
a.why: The published result is an equivalence between being a norm and the vanishing of the cyclic algebra class, and the Lean statement gives one direction at the level of cocycles.

b.states: Let K be a field with separable closure Ω, N > 0, ζ a primitive N-th root of unity in Ω with cyclotomic character c0 modulo N, ψ a continuous homomorphism from Gal(Ω/K) to ℤ/N, and U in K^× a norm from the fixed field of the kernel of ψ. For any T in Ω with T^N = U and any κ with g(T) = ζ^{κ(g)}·T for all g, there is a locally constant map c from the Galois group to ℤ/N with c0(g)·c(h) − c(gh) + c(g) = κ(g)·ψ(h) for all g and h. This says that the cup product of the Kummer class of U with ψ is zero in H²(K, ℤ/N(1)).
b.known_as: The norm criterion for cyclic algebras in cup product form, by which the cup product of the Kummer class of U with ψ, the class of the cyclic algebra (ψ, U), vanishes when U is a norm from the cyclic extension cut out by ψ (Serre, Local Fields XIV, Gille–Szamuely 4.7)

check.known_as: the norm criterion for cyclic algebras in the direction that a norm U from the cyclic extension cut out by ψ makes the class of the cyclic algebra (ψ, U) vanish, here written as the cup product of the Kummer class of U with ψ in H²(K, μ_N) (Serre, Local Fields XIV §1)
check.vacuity: None found, although the hypothesis of a primitive N-th root of unity in Ω can be met only when the characteristic of K does not divide N.
check.note: The maps c0 and κ are determined by ζ and T, so their hypotheses only fix notation, and the conclusion is a cocycle identity with a locally constant cochain c rather than a statement about classes.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.KummerCup.exists_lift_of_norm
theorems.areas: topology, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let K be a field with separable closure Ω and Galois group G, let N ≥ 1, let ψ be a homomorphism from G to Z/N with open kernel, and let U ∈ K^× be a norm from the fixed field L of ker ψ. Write ψ̄(g) ∈ {0, …, N − 1} for the representative of ψ(g). Then there is a locally constant map b from G to Ω^× with g(b(h)) b(g) = U^{⌊(ψ̄(g) + ψ̄(h))/N⌋} b(gh) for all g, h ∈ G. The 2-cocycle U^{⌊(ψ̄(g) + ψ̄(h))/N⌋} represents the cyclic algebra (ψ, U) in Br(K) = H²(G, Ω^×), so the statement says that this class is zero.
a.notation: U ∈ N_{L/K}(L^×) ⟹ ∃ b ∈ C⁰(G, Ω^×) with U^{⌊(ψ̄(g)+ψ̄(h))/N⌋} = g(b(h)) b(g) b(gh)⁻¹ for all g, h
a.known_as: the norm criterion for the splitting of a cyclic algebra, in the direction that a norm b from L_χ gives (χ, b) = b ∪ δχ = 0 in Br(K)
a.reference: J.-P. Serre, Local Fields, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 67, 1979
a.why: Serre proves for any field that b is a norm from L_χ exactly when b ∪ δχ vanishes, and the Lean statement is the forward direction written with the standard cocycle of δχ.

b.states: Let K be a field with separable closure Ω, N a nonzero natural number, ψ a continuous homomorphism from Gal(Ω/K) to ℤ/N, and U in K^× a norm from the fixed field of the kernel of ψ. Then there is a locally constant map b from the Galois group to Ω^× with g(b(h))·b(g) = U^{⌊(ψ(g) + ψ(h))/N⌋}·b(gh) for all g and h, where ψ(g) and ψ(h) are read as integers in {0, …, N − 1}. In other words, the standard 2-cocycle of the cyclic algebra (ψ, U) is a coboundary in H²(K, Ω^×).
b.known_as: A cyclic algebra (L/K, ψ, U) splits when U is a norm from L, the easy direction of the isomorphism Br(L/K) ≅ K^×/N(L^×) for a cyclic extension L of K

check.known_as: the splitting of the cyclic algebra (ψ, U) when U is a norm from the cyclic extension cut out by ψ, the easy direction of the isomorphism of K^×/N(L^×) with Br(L/K) for a cyclic extension L/K (Serre, Local Fields XIV §1)
check.note: The cocycle U^{⌊(ψ̄(g) + ψ̄(h))/N⌋} is the cup product of U with the coboundary of ψ/N in H²(G, ℤ), and ψ need not be onto ℤ/N, so the fixed field of its kernel can have any degree dividing N.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.oddWeight_modular_cusp_dimension_lower_bound
theorems.areas: modular forms, linear algebra, group theory

a.states: Let N ≥ 5 and M ≥ 1, let Γ be a subgroup of SL₂(Z) with Γ(M) ⊆ Γ ⊆ Γ₁(N), and let k ≥ 3 be odd. Then the complex spaces M_k(Γ) of modular forms and S_k(Γ) of cusp forms of weight k are finite-dimensional, and k − 1 times the index of Γ in SL₂(Z) is at most 12 (dim M_k(Γ) + dim S_k(Γ)).
a.notation: Γ(M) ⊆ Γ ⊆ Γ₁(N), N ≥ 5, k ≥ 3 odd ⟹ dim M_k(Γ), dim S_k(Γ) < ∞ and (k − 1)[SL₂(Z) : Γ] ≤ 12 (dim_C M_k(Γ) + dim_C S_k(Γ))
a.known_as: the dimension formulas for modular and cusp forms of odd weight combined with the genus formula, which for such Γ give equality
a.reference: F. Diamond and J. Shurman, A First Course in Modular Forms, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 228, 2005
a.why: For N ≥ 5 the group Γ omits −I and has no elliptic points and no irregular cusps, so the textbook formulas give dim M_k + dim S_k = (k − 1)(2g − 2 + ε_∞), which the genus formula turns into (k − 1) times the index divided by 12, but the inequality itself is not a textbook statement.

b.states: For natural numbers N ≥ 5 and M > 0, a subgroup Γ of SL(2, ℤ) with Γ(M) ≤ Γ ≤ Γ1(N), and an odd weight k ≥ 3, the spaces of modular forms and of cusp forms of weight k for Γ are finite dimensional, and k − 1 times the index of Γ in SL(2, ℤ) is at most 12 times the sum of their dimensions.
b.known_as: The dimension formulas for modular forms and cusp forms of odd weight (Shimura, Diamond–Shurman Theorem 3.6.1) together with the genus formula, which for such Γ, having no elliptic points, no −I and only regular cusps, give the equality of 12(dim M_k + dim S_k) with k − 1 times the index

check.known_as: the dimension formulas for modular and cusp forms of odd weight k ≥ 3 on a group without −I, elliptic points or irregular cusps, combined with the genus formula (Shimura, Introduction to the Arithmetic Theory of Automorphic Functions, Chapter 2, and Diamond–Shurman, Chapter 3), which give that 12(dim M_k + dim S_k) equals k − 1 times the index of Γ in SL₂(ℤ)
check.vacuity: None found, though the chain Γ(M) ≤ Γ ≤ Γ₁(N) can be met only when N divides M, for example with Γ = Γ₁(N) and M = N.
check.note: The index is taken in SL₂(ℤ), which is twice the index of the image of Γ in PSL₂(ℤ) because Γ omits −I, and with that index the inequality is in fact an equality.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_base_element_negative_at_two_embeddings
theorems.areas: number fields, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let L/K be a quadratic extension of number fields with a ring endomorphism σ ≠ id of L that fixes K and satisfies φ(σx) = conj φ(x) for every complex embedding φ of L. These conditions force K to be totally real and L to be totally imaginary, so L is a CM field with totally real subfield K. Let ε and ε′ be complex embeddings of L with ε′ ≠ ε and ε′ ≠ ε̄, so that they lie over two distinct real places of K. Then there is a nonzero h ∈ K such that ε(h) and ε′(h) have negative real part, φ(h) has positive real part for every embedding φ outside {ε, ε̄, ε′, ε̄′}, and h is a norm from K_v ⊗_K L to K_v at every finite place v of K.
a.notation: L/K CM quadratic, ε, ε′ over distinct real places ⟹ ∃ h ∈ K^× with ε(h), ε′(h) < 0, φ(h) > 0 for φ ∉ {ε, ε̄, ε′, ε̄′}, h ∈ N(K_v ⊗_K L) for every finite v
a.known_as: existence of a global element with prescribed local Hilbert symbols, here an element that is a local norm from L at every place of K except the two real places below ε and ε′
a.reference: O. T. O'Meara, Introduction to Quadratic Forms, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 117, 1963, §71
a.why: The conditions say that the Hilbert symbol of h for L/K is −1 exactly at the two given real places, an even set that the cited existence theorem allows, but the form with two named embeddings is shaped for one use.

b.states: Let L be a quadratic extension of a number field K with an automorphism σ ≠ id fixing K that every complex embedding of L turns into complex conjugation, so that L is a CM field with totally real subfield K, and let ε and ε' be complex embeddings of L with ε ≠ ε' and ε ≠ conj(ε'), so that they lie over different real places of K. Then there is a nonzero h in K that is negative under ε and ε', positive under every complex embedding other than ε, conj(ε), ε' and conj(ε'), and a norm from the algebra K_v ⊗_K L at every finite place v of K.
b.known_as: The existence of a global element with prescribed local Hilbert symbols (O'Meara 71:19, Serre's A Course in Arithmetic III Theorem 4 over ℚ), applied to L/K with symbol −1 at exactly two real places and +1 at every other place
b.vacuity: The hypotheses can be met only when K has at least two real embeddings, so the statement is empty for K = ℚ but not in general.

check.known_as: the existence of a global element with prescribed local Hilbert symbols (O'Meara, Introduction to Quadratic Forms, §71, and Serre, A Course in Arithmetic III Theorem 4 over ℚ), applied to the CM extension L/K with symbol −1 at exactly the two real places below ε and ε′ and +1 at every other place
check.note: The hypotheses on ε and ε′ can be met only when K has at least two real places, so the case K = ℚ is empty, and the norm condition at a finite place v is stated for the algebra K_v ⊗_K L, which is K_v × K_v when v splits in L.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.QuadSigns.exists_signs
theorems.areas: number fields, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let L/K be a quadratic extension of number fields with a ring endomorphism σ ≠ id of L that fixes K and satisfies φ(σx) = conj φ(x) for every complex embedding φ of L. These conditions force K to be totally real and L to be totally imaginary, so L is a CM field with totally real subfield K. Let ε and ε′ be complex embeddings of L with ε′ ≠ ε and ε′ ≠ ε̄, so that they lie over two distinct real places of K. Then there is a nonzero h ∈ K such that ε(h) and ε′(h) have negative real part, φ(h) has positive real part for every embedding φ outside {ε, ε̄, ε′, ε̄′}, and h is a norm from K_v ⊗_K L to K_v at every finite place v of K.
a.notation: L/K CM quadratic, ε, ε′ over distinct real places ⟹ ∃ h ∈ K^× with ε(h), ε′(h) < 0, φ(h) > 0 for φ ∉ {ε, ε̄, ε′, ε̄′}, h ∈ N(K_v ⊗_K L) for every finite v
a.known_as: existence of a global element with prescribed local Hilbert symbols, here an element that is a local norm from L at every place of K except the two real places below ε and ε′
a.reference: O. T. O'Meara, Introduction to Quadratic Forms, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 117, 1963, §71
a.why: Its statement is identical to that of theorem 33, a special case of the cited existence theorem for an even set of two real places, shaped for one use.

b.states: The statement is that of Theorem 33 with the hypotheses named. For a quadratic extension L of a number field K with an automorphism σ ≠ id fixing K that every complex embedding turns into complex conjugation, and complex embeddings ε, ε' of L with ε ≠ ε' and ε ≠ conj(ε'), there is a nonzero h in K that is negative under ε and ε', positive under every complex embedding other than ε, conj(ε), ε' and conj(ε'), and a norm from K_v ⊗_K L at every finite place v of K.
b.known_as: The existence of a global element with prescribed local Hilbert symbols (O'Meara 71:19, Serre's A Course in Arithmetic III Theorem 4 over ℚ), applied to L/K with symbol −1 at exactly two real places and +1 at every other place
b.vacuity: The hypotheses can be met only when K has at least two real embeddings, so the statement is empty for K = ℚ but not in general.

check.known_as: the existence of a global element with prescribed local Hilbert symbols (O'Meara, Introduction to Quadratic Forms, §71, and Serre, A Course in Arithmetic III Theorem 4 over ℚ), applied to the CM extension L/K with symbol −1 at exactly the two real places below ε and ε′ and +1 at every other place
check.note: The Lean statement is that of number 33 with the hypotheses named, and its hypotheses on ε and ε′ can be met only when K has at least two real places.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.JR.WeilQuad.NormSign.mul_norm_of_not_norm
theorems.areas: other number theory, topology, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero and L a field extension of K of degree 2. If s, t ∈ K^× are both not norms of elements of L, then st is the norm of an element of L.
a.known_as: the norm index theorem for quadratic extensions of local fields, by which N_{L/K}(L^×) has index 2 in K^×
a.reference: J.-P. Serre, Local Fields, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 67, 1979
a.why: The norm group of a quadratic extension of a local field has index exactly 2, and the Lean statement uses only that the index is at most 2.

b.states: Let K be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero and L a field that is a K-algebra of dimension 2. If s and t in K^× are both not norms from L, then their product s·t is a norm from L.
b.known_as: The norm group of a quadratic extension of a local field has index 2 in K^×, from local class field theory or from the multiplicativity of the Hilbert symbol

check.known_as: the fact that the norm group of a quadratic extension of a local field has index 2 in K^×, from local class field theory or the nondegeneracy of the Hilbert symbol
check.note: Only the bound of at most 2 on the index enters the Lean conclusion, and the hypothesis CharZero K is more than that bound needs.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.LandherrSignature.congr_of_det_norm
theorems.areas: number fields, linear algebra, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let E be a CM number field with its complex conjugation as the star operation, and let G and G′ be n × n matrices over E that are Hermitian for this conjugation and have nonzero determinant. Suppose that det G = z z̄ det G′ for some z ∈ E, and that for every embedding τ of E into C there is a nonsingular complex matrix Q with Q* τ(G) Q = τ(G′), which by Sylvester's law of inertia says that G and G′ have the same signature at every embedding. Then there is a nonsingular matrix P over E with P* G P = G′.
a.notation: G* = G, G′* = G′, det G ∈ N_{E/E⁺}(E) · det G′, τ(G) ≅ τ(G′) over C for all τ ⟹ ∃ P ∈ GL_n(E) with P* G P = G′
a.known_as: Landherr's theorem on the classification of Hermitian forms over number fields by rank, determinant modulo norms and signatures
a.reference: W. Landherr, Äquivalenz Hermitescher Formen über einem beliebigen algebraischen Zahlkörper, Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg 11, 1936
a.why: Landherr's theorem classifies nondegenerate Hermitian forms over any quadratic extension of number fields by rank, determinant modulo norms and signatures at the real places that become complex, and for a CM field every real place of the totally real subfield is of that kind.

b.states: Let E be a CM number field and G, G' nonsingular hermitian n × n matrices over E whose determinants satisfy det G = z·z̄·det G' for some z in E. If for every complex embedding τ of E there is an invertible complex matrix Q with Qᴴ·G^τ·Q = G'^τ, which means that the two forms have the same signature at every infinite place, then there is an invertible matrix P over E with Pᴴ·G·P = G'.
b.known_as: Landherr's theorem that hermitian forms over a quadratic extension of number fields are classified by rank, determinant modulo norms and signatures at the real places

check.known_as: Landherr's theorem that nondegenerate hermitian forms over a quadratic extension of number fields are classified by rank, determinant modulo norms and signatures at the real places that become complex (Landherr 1936, Scharlau, Quadratic and Hermitian Forms, Chapter 10)
check.note: The Lean text gives only the sufficiency direction for a CM field over its totally real subfield, and it states the signature condition as congruence over ℂ at every complex embedding, which by Sylvester's law of inertia means equal signatures.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_eliminationForm_generalLinearForms_cone
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let F be a field of characteristic zero, I a homogeneous prime ideal of F[x₁, …, x_N] whose quotient ring has Krull dimension D + 1 with D ≥ 1, and g a homogeneous polynomial of degree d with g ∉ I. Then there is a nonzero polynomial Q over F in the D·N coefficients s_{ij} of D linear forms with the following property for every field extension K of F. If the D linear forms with coefficients s ∈ K^{D×N} have a common nonzero zero y ∈ K^N on which every element of I and g vanish, then Q(s) = 0. Geometrically, the D-tuples of linear forms whose common zero set meets the projective variety V(I) ∩ V(g) of dimension D − 1 lie in a hypersurface.
a.known_as: existence of the Chow form, or elimination form, of a projective variety, by which the linear subspaces of complementary dimension that meet the variety form a hypersurface
a.reference: I. M. Gelfand, M. M. Kapranov and A. V. Zelevinsky, Discriminants, Resultants, and Multidimensional Determinants, 1994
a.why: For the variety V(I) ∩ V(g) of dimension D − 1 the Chow form is a nonzero polynomial in the coefficients of D linear forms that vanishes exactly when they have a common zero on the variety, and the Lean statement keeps only the vanishing.

b.states: Let F be a field of characteristic zero, I a homogeneous prime ideal of F[x_1, …, x_N] whose quotient ring has Krull dimension D + 1 with D ≥ 1, and g a homogeneous polynomial of degree d that is not in I. Then there is a nonzero polynomial Q in the D·N coefficients of D linear forms such that for every field K over F and all D linear forms s over K, if some nonzero y in K^N is a zero of every element of I, of g and of all D forms, then Q vanishes at the coefficients of s.
b.known_as: The existence of an elimination form of Chow form type for the projective variety cut out by I and g, which has dimension D − 1, equivalently the fact that D general hyperplanes miss that variety (elimination theory as in Nesterenko and Philippon, Shafarevich's Basic Algebraic Geometry I.6)
b.vacuity: None found, and the case d = 0 holds trivially because g is then a nonzero constant.

check.known_as: the existence of an eliminating form of Chow form type for the projective variety V(I) ∩ V(g) of dimension D − 1, by which the D-tuples of hyperplanes that meet a projective variety of dimension D − 1 lie in a hypersurface (Shafarevich, Basic Algebraic Geometry I.6, and the elimination theory of Nesterenko and Philippon)
check.vacuity: None found, and for d = 0 the polynomial g is a nonzero constant, so that case holds with any nonzero Q.
check.note: The Lean text keeps only the vanishing of Q on the tuples that meet the variety and leaves out the converse and the irreducibility of the Chow form, and the hypothesis of characteristic zero is more than the published fact needs.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.homogeneous_correction_next_level_alt
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal of R and K₀, K₁, … ideals of R[X₀, …, X_n] with three properties. Each K_e contains every homogeneous F for which each X_i has a power with X_i^N F ∈ K_e, each K_e contains the constants from I^{e+1}, and for every homogeneous F ∈ K_e of degree t and every i there are N and a homogeneous G of degree t + N with coefficients in I^{e+1} such that X_i^N F − G ∈ K_{e+1}. Then there is t₀ such that for every t ≥ t₀, every e and every homogeneous F ∈ K_e of degree t there is a homogeneous G of degree t with coefficients in I^{e+1} and F − G ∈ K_{e+1}.
a.notation: (K_e saturated, I^{e+1} ⊆ K_e, ∀ F ∈ (K_e)_t ∀ i ∃ N, G_i ∈ (I^{e+1}R[X])_{t+N} with X_i^N F − G_i ∈ K_{e+1}) ⟹ ∃ t₀ ∀ t ≥ t₀ ∀ e ∀ F ∈ (K_e)_t ∃ G ∈ (I^{e+1}R[X])_t with F − G ∈ K_{e+1}
a.known_as: no published result known, a gluing lemma of Serre vanishing type that turns corrections on the standard affine charts of projective space into one global correction in large degree, uniformly in e
a.why: The hypotheses form an abstract interface for a filtration by ideals and the degree bound uniform in e is the kind of conclusion that Serre's vanishing theorem gives, which marks the statement as a step tailored to one proof.

b.states: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal of R and K_e for e in ℕ ideals of R[X_0, …, X_n] such that a homogeneous F lies in K_e whenever X_i^N·F lies in K_e for every i, every constant from I^{e+1} lies in K_e, and for each homogeneous F of degree t in K_e and each i some X_i^N·F differs modulo K_{e+1} from a homogeneous polynomial of degree t + N with coefficients in I^{e+1}. Then there is t₀ such that for all t ≥ t₀, all e and every homogeneous F of degree t in K_e there is a homogeneous G of degree t with coefficients in I^{e+1} and F − G in K_{e+1}.
b.known_as: A form of Serre's theorem that a finitely generated graded module agrees in large degrees with the global sections of the twists of its sheaf (EGA II 2.7.3, Hartshorne II Exercise 5.9), made uniform in e through finite generation over the Rees algebra as in the proof of the theorem on formal functions

check.known_as: no published result known, a gluing lemma that in every large degree t, uniformly in e, writes each homogeneous element of K_e modulo K_{e+1} as one with coefficients in I^{e+1}, a consequence of Serre's theorem on graded modules applied over the associated graded ring of I
check.note: The three hypotheses together give I·K_e ⊆ K_{e+1} on homogeneous elements, and this inclusion is what lets a single bound t₀ serve every e.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.uniform_serre_sections_alt
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal of R and J₀, J₁, … ideals of R[X₀, …, X_n] such that a F ∈ J_{e+1} whenever a ∈ I and F is a homogeneous polynomial in J_e with coefficients in I^e. Then there is d₀ such that the following holds for every d ≥ d₀, every e and every N. If F₀, …, F_n are homogeneous of degree d + N with coefficients in I^e and for all i, j some power of X_i X_j times X_j^N F_i − X_i^N F_j lies in J_e, then there is a homogeneous G of degree d with coefficients in I^e such that for each i some power of X_i times F_i − X_i^N G lies in J_e. In sheaf language, compatible local sections F_i / X_i^N on the charts D₊(X_i) come from one homogeneous polynomial of degree d, with d₀ independent of e and N.
a.notation: ∃ d₀ ∀ d ≥ d₀ ∀ e, N ∀ F_i ∈ (I^e R[X])_{d+N} ((X_iX_j)^L (X_j^N F_i − X_i^N F_j) ∈ J_e ∀ i, j ⟹ ∃ G ∈ (I^e R[X])_d with X_i^L (F_i − X_i^N G) ∈ J_e ∀ i)
a.known_as: no published result known, a version of Serre's theorem that M_d → Γ(ℙ^n, M̃(d)) is surjective for large d, made uniform over the modules I^e R[X] modulo J_e
a.why: For a single e the conclusion is Serre's surjectivity of M_d onto the global sections of M̃(d) for large d, but the uniformity over e and the abstract hypothesis on the ideals J_e are tailored to the project.

b.states: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal of R and J_e for e in ℕ ideals of R[X_0, …, X_n] such that a·F lies in J_{e+1} whenever a is in I and F is a homogeneous element of J_e with coefficients in I^e. Then there is d₀ such that for all d ≥ d₀, all e and N, and all homogeneous F_0, …, F_n of degree d + N with coefficients in I^e that satisfy (X_i·X_j)^L·(X_j^N·F_i − X_i^N·F_j) ∈ J_e for some L, there is a homogeneous G of degree d with coefficients in I^e such that X_i^L·(F_i − X_i^N·G) ∈ J_e for each i and some L.
b.known_as: Serre's theorem that for a finitely generated graded module M the map from M_d to the global sections of the twisted sheaf is onto for large d (EGA II 2.7.3, Hartshorne II Exercise 5.9), applied over the Rees algebra so that the bound is uniform in e

check.known_as: Serre's theorem that for a finitely generated graded module M over a polynomial ring over a Noetherian base the map M_d → Γ(ℙ^n, M̃(d)) is onto for large d (Serre's FAC, Hartshorne II Exercise 5.9), applied to the modules I^e R[X] modulo J_e assembled over the Rees algebra of I so that the bound is uniform in e
check.note: The hypothesis that a·F lies in J_{e+1} for a in I and homogeneous F in J_e with coefficients in I^e is what makes the direct sum of these modules a module over the Rees algebra, and the bound d₀ is uniform in N as well as in e.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.ProfCoh.subsingleton_groupCohomology_three_of_tate
theorems.areas: representation theory, category theory, group theory, homological algebra

a.states: Let Γ be a finite group, M a Γ-module and u ∈ H²(Γ, M). Suppose that for every subgroup S of Γ the group H¹(S, M) is zero, the restriction of u to S has additive order |S|, and every element of H²(S, M) is an integer multiple of that restriction. Then H³(Γ, M) = 0.
a.notation: ∀ S ≤ Γ (H¹(S, M) = 0, H²(S, M) = ⟨res_S u⟩ ≅ Z/|S|) ⟹ H³(Γ, M) = 0
a.known_as: Tate's theorem on cup product with a fundamental class, which gives H³(Γ, M) ≅ Ĥ¹(Γ, Z) = Hom(Γ, Z) = 0
a.reference: J. Tate, The higher dimensional cohomology groups of class field theory, Annals of Mathematics 56, 1952
a.why: Under exactly these hypotheses Tate's theorem gives isomorphisms Ĥ^n(Γ, Z) ≅ Ĥ^{n+2}(Γ, M), and the case n = 1 yields the Lean conclusion because a finite group has no nonzero homomorphism to Z.

b.states: Let Γ be a finite group, M a ℤ[Γ]-module and u an element of H²(Γ, M). Suppose that for every subgroup S the group H¹(S, M) is zero, the restriction of u to S has additive order equal to the order of S, and every element of H²(S, M) is an integer multiple of that restriction. Then H³(Γ, M) has at most one element.
b.known_as: A consequence of Tate's theorem (Tate–Nakayama), by which cup product with u gives isomorphisms from Ĥ^n(Γ, ℤ) to Ĥ^{n+2}(Γ, M), here at n = 1 where Ĥ¹(Γ, ℤ) = Hom(Γ, ℤ) = 0

check.known_as: Tate's theorem on cup product with a fundamental class (Tate–Nakayama), by which cup product with u gives isomorphisms from Ĥ^n(Γ, ℤ) to Ĥ^{n+2}(Γ, M), here at n = 1 where Ĥ¹(Γ, ℤ) = Hom(Γ, ℤ) = 0
check.note: The hypotheses on u say that for every subgroup S the group H²(S, M) is cyclic of order |S| and generated by the restriction of u, which are exactly Tate's hypotheses, and the Lean conclusion is only the case n = 1.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.ProfCoh.subsingleton_groupCohomology_three_of_tate_int
theorems.areas: representation theory, category theory, group theory, homological algebra

a.states: Let Γ be a finite group, M a representation of Γ over ℤ and u a class in H²(Γ, M). Assume that for every subgroup S of Γ the group H¹(S, M) is zero, the restriction of u to H²(S, M) has additive order equal to the order of S, and every element of H²(S, M) is an integer multiple of that restriction. Then H³(Γ, M) has at most one element, so it is the zero group.
a.notation: Γ finite, M ∈ Rep_ℤ(Γ), u ∈ H²(Γ,M), and for all S ≤ Γ, H¹(S,M) = 0, ord(res_S u) = |S|, H²(S,M) = ℤ·res_S u ⟹ H³(Γ,M) = 0
a.known_as: the degree-three case of Tate's theorem, in which cup product with u gives an isomorphism Ĥ¹(Γ,ℤ) ≅ H³(Γ,M) and Ĥ¹(Γ,ℤ) = Hom(Γ,ℤ) vanishes because Γ is finite
a.reference: J. Tate, The higher dimensional cohomology groups of class field theory, Annals of Mathematics 56 (1952)
a.why: Under these hypotheses Tate's theorem gives isomorphisms Ĥ^q(Γ,ℤ) ≅ Ĥ^{q+2}(Γ,M) for every q, and the Lean statement keeps only the vanishing that the case q = 1 yields, so it follows from the theorem and claims less.

b.states: For a finite group Γ, a representation M of Γ over ℤ and a class u in H²(Γ, M), the statement assumes three conditions for every subgroup S of Γ. The group H¹(S, M) is zero, the restriction of u to H²(S, M) has additive order equal to the cardinality of S, and every element of H²(S, M) is an integer multiple of that restriction. Under these hypotheses H³(Γ, M) has at most one element, so it is the zero group.
b.known_as: Tate's theorem (Tate–Nakayama) on a class in H² whose restrictions generate H² of every subgroup with order equal to the subgroup's order, through its consequence H³(G, M) ≅ Ĥ¹(G, ℤ) = Hom(G, ℤ) = 0

check.known_as: the degree-three case of Tate's theorem on a class in H² whose restrictions generate H² of every subgroup with order equal to the subgroup's order (Tate 1952), which gives H³(Γ, M) ≅ Ĥ¹(Γ, ℤ) = Hom(Γ, ℤ) = 0
check.note: The hypotheses are exactly those of Tate's theorem taken at every subgroup, and the Lean statement keeps only the vanishing of H³ that the isomorphism Ĥ¹(Γ, ℤ) ≅ H³(Γ, M) gives.

theorems.name: ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.L1.unit_prod
theorems.areas: p-adic numbers, special functions, other analysis, topology, field theory

a.states: Let L be a lattice in ℂ with Weierstrass invariants g₂, g₃ and Weierstrass function ℘, let l ≥ 5 be a prime, ι a field isomorphism from ℂ to ℂ_l, and μ ∈ ℂ_l with μ¹²ι(g₂³ − 27g₃²) = 1, |μ⁴ι(g₂)| ≤ 1 and |μ⁶ι(g₃)| ≤ 1. Let e and N be natural numbers such that e = 3 and |μ⁴ι(g₂)| < 1, or e = 2 and |μ⁶ι(g₃)| < 1, and such that neither l nor e divides N. Then for every finite set T of complex numbers z with z ∉ L and Nz ∈ L, the product |μ|^{2|T|}·|ι(∏_{z∈T} ℘(z))| of l-adic absolute values equals 1. The hypotheses on μ say that the model y² = 4x³ − μ⁴ι(g₂)x − μ⁶ι(g₃) of the curve has good reduction at l, with reduced j-invariant 0 when e = 3 and 1728 when e = 2.
a.notation: l ≥ 5 prime, μ¹²ι(g₂³−27g₃²) = 1, |μ⁴ιg₂|, |μ⁶ιg₃| ≤ 1, (e = 3 and |μ⁴ιg₂| < 1) or (e = 2 and |μ⁶ιg₃| < 1), l ∤ N, e ∤ N, T ⊂ N⁻¹L ∖ L finite ⟹ |μ|^{2|T|}·|ι(∏_{z∈T} ℘_L(z))|_l = 1
a.known_as: the product over a finite set of nonzero N-torsion points of the unit statement of Theorem 43, which rests on the integrality of torsion points of order prime to l on an elliptic curve with good reduction and on the injectivity of reduction on such torsion
a.reference: J. H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 1986
a.why: The statement is the product of the unit statements of Theorem 43 over the points of T and is clearly shaped for one computation, but no published text states it in this form, so the relation word is a judgement.

b.states: Let L be a period pair with lattice in ℂ, l a prime with 5 ≤ l, ι a ring isomorphism from ℂ onto ℂ_l, and μ in ℂ_l with μ¹²·ι(g₂³ − 27g₃²) = 1, ‖μ⁴·ι(g₂)‖ ≤ 1 and ‖μ⁶·ι(g₃)‖ ≤ 1. Let e and N be natural numbers with either e = 3 and ‖μ⁴·ι(g₂)‖ < 1 or e = 2 and ‖μ⁶·ι(g₃)‖ < 1, and with neither l nor e dividing N. Then for every finite set T of complex numbers that lie outside the lattice and whose product with N lies in the lattice, ‖μ‖^(2·|T|) · ‖ι(∏_{z∈T} ℘(z))‖ = 1, where ℘ is the Weierstrass function of L.
b.known_as: no published result known
b.vacuity: None found, although the conclusion follows at once from Theorem 43 by multiplicativity of the l-adic norm, and the hypotheses are met for example by the hexagonal lattice with g₂ = 0, e = 3 and N = 2.

check.known_as: no published result known, a product form of the lemma that the rescaled x-coordinates of the nonzero N-torsion points of an elliptic curve with good reduction at l and reduced j-invariant 0 or 1728 are l-adic units
check.note: The statement follows from Theorem 43 by the multiplicativity of ι and of the l-adic norm, and the hypotheses can be met, for example by the hexagonal lattice with g₂ = 0, e = 3 and N = 2.

theorems.name: ReciprocityTheory.ChartRestriction.L1.unit_point
theorems.areas: p-adic numbers, special functions, other analysis, topology, field theory

a.states: Let L be a lattice in ℂ with Weierstrass invariants g₂, g₃ and Weierstrass function ℘, let l ≥ 5 be a prime, ι a field isomorphism from ℂ to ℂ_l, and μ ∈ ℂ_l with μ¹²ι(g₂³ − 27g₃²) = 1, |μ⁴ι(g₂)| ≤ 1 and |μ⁶ι(g₃)| ≤ 1. Let e and N be natural numbers such that e = 3 and |μ⁴ι(g₂)| < 1, or e = 2 and |μ⁶ι(g₃)| < 1, and such that neither l nor e divides N. Then every complex number z with z ∉ L and Nz ∈ L satisfies |μ²ι(℘(z))| = 1 for the l-adic absolute value. In terms of the model y² = 4x³ − μ⁴ι(g₂)x − μ⁶ι(g₃), which has good reduction at l, the x-coordinate of every nonzero N-torsion point is an l-adic unit.
a.notation: l ≥ 5 prime, μ¹²ι(g₂³−27g₃²) = 1, |μ⁴ιg₂|, |μ⁶ιg₃| ≤ 1, (e = 3 and |μ⁴ιg₂| < 1) or (e = 2 and |μ⁶ιg₃| < 1), l ∤ N, e ∤ N, z ∉ L, Nz ∈ L ⟹ |μ²ι(℘_L(z))|_l = 1
a.known_as: the integrality of torsion points of order prime to l on an elliptic curve with good reduction and the injectivity of reduction on such torsion, combined with the fact that the points with x = 0 on the reduced curve have order 3 when j = 0 and order 2 when j = 1728
a.reference: J. H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 1986
a.why: Integrality gives |μ²ι(℘(z))| ≤ 1, and a reduced x-coordinate 0 would make the reduced point a point of order 3 or 2 dividing N, which the hypotheses exclude, so the statement is a specific consequence of the published results and not one of them.

b.states: Let L be a period pair, l a prime with 5 ≤ l, ι a ring isomorphism from ℂ onto ℂ_l and μ in ℂ_l with μ¹²·ι(g₂³ − 27g₃²) = 1, ‖μ⁴·ι(g₂)‖ ≤ 1 and ‖μ⁶·ι(g₃)‖ ≤ 1. Let e and N be natural numbers with e = 3 and ‖μ⁴·ι(g₂)‖ < 1 or with e = 2 and ‖μ⁶·ι(g₃)‖ < 1, and with neither l nor e dividing N. Then every complex z outside the lattice of L with N·z in the lattice satisfies ‖μ²·ι(℘(z))‖ = 1, which says that the rescaled x-coordinate of each nonzero N-torsion point is an l-adic unit.
b.known_as: no published result known

check.known_as: no published result known, a lemma that combines the injectivity of reduction on torsion of order prime to l for an elliptic curve with good reduction (Silverman, AEC VII.3.1) with the orders of the points with x = 0 on reduced curves with j-invariant 0 or 1728
check.note: The hypotheses on μ say that the rescaled model y² = 4x³ − μ⁴ι(g₂)x − μ⁶ι(g₃) has good reduction at l with reduced j-invariant 0 when e = 3 and 1728 when e = 2, and the condition that e does not divide N excludes the torsion points that reduce to a point with x = 0, which have order 3 or 2.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.UU.SpecialPairing.torsion_ext
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics

a.states: Let W be a local ring that is complete for its maximal ideal, S a scheme, G a smooth commutative group scheme over S, p a morphism from Spec W to S, and N a natural number that is a unit in W. Let f be a local ring homomorphism from W to a field Ω, so that Spec Ω maps to the closed point of Spec W. If two W-points y and y' of G over p satisfy y^N = 1 and y'^N = 1 and agree after composition with the morphism Spec Ω → Spec W induced by f, then y = y'.
a.notation: G/S smooth commutative group scheme, W complete local, N ∈ W^×, f ∈ Hom_loc(W, Ω), y, y' ∈ G(W) over p, y^N = y'^N = 1, y ∘ Spec f = y' ∘ Spec f ⟹ y = y'
a.known_as: injectivity of reduction on torsion of order invertible in the base for a smooth commutative group scheme over a local ring, which holds because the N-torsion subgroup scheme is étale
a.reference: S. Bosch, W. Lütkebohmert and M. Raynaud, Néron Models, 1990
a.why: The published fact needs only a local ring in which N is invertible, so the completeness hypothesis narrows the setting, and I am not certain of the exact textbook location of the statement for general smooth commutative group schemes.

b.states: Let W be a local ring that is complete and separated for the adic topology of its maximal ideal, S a scheme, G a commutative group object over S with smooth structure morphism, p a morphism from Spec W to S, and N a natural number whose image in W is a unit. Let f be a local ring homomorphism from W to a field Ω, and let y and y' be morphisms over S from Spec W to G with y^N = 1 and y'^N = 1 in the group of such morphisms. If y and y' become equal after composition with the morphism Spec Ω → Spec W induced by f, then y = y'.
b.known_as: injectivity of reduction on N-torsion points when N is invertible on the base, which comes from the étaleness of the N-torsion of a smooth commutative group scheme (for elliptic curves Silverman, AEC VII Prop. 3.1)

check.known_as: injectivity of reduction on N-torsion points of a smooth commutative group scheme over a local ring in which N is invertible, which comes from the étaleness of the N-torsion subgroup scheme
check.note: The completeness of W is not needed for this uniqueness, because the N-torsion of G is unramified over Spec W and two points of an unramified scheme over a local base that agree at the closed point agree everywhere.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.etale_atPrime_of_regular_of_isIntegrallyClosedIn
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, group theory

a.states: Let R be a domain and C a commutative R-algebra that is finite as an R-module and integrally closed in its localization at the nonzero elements of R. Let P be a prime of R such that the localization R_P is a regular local ring. If C ⊗_R R_{P'} is étale over R_{P'} for every prime P' ⊆ P of height at most one, then C ⊗_R R_P is étale over R_P.
a.notation: R domain, C finite R-algebra integrally closed in C ⊗_R Frac(R), R_P regular, C_{P'} étale over R_{P'} for all primes P' ⊆ P with ht P' ≤ 1 ⟹ C_P étale over R_P
a.known_as: the Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus
a.reference: M. Nagata, On the purity of branch loci in regular local rings, Illinois Journal of Mathematics 3 (1959)
a.vacuity: When P itself has height at most one the conclusion is the hypothesis at P' = P, and for P of height at least two none found.
a.why: The hypothesis at P' = 0 makes C ⊗ Frac(R) a finite étale algebra, so C_P is the integral closure of the regular local ring R_P in a finite étale algebra over its fraction field, which is exactly the setting of purity of the branch locus.

b.states: For every domain R and every finite R-algebra C that is integrally closed in its localization at the images of the nonzero elements of R, and for every prime P of R whose localization R_P is a regular local ring, the statement assumes that R_{P'} ⊗_R C is étale over R_{P'} for every prime P' contained in P with height at most 1. Under this hypothesis R_P ⊗_R C is étale over R_P.
b.known_as: Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus, which says that a finite normal cover of a regular local scheme that is étale in codimension one is étale
b.vacuity: When P has height at most 1 the conclusion is the hypothesis taken at P' = P, but for larger height the hypotheses can be met and the conclusion is not immediate.

check.known_as: Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus
check.vacuity: None found, although when P has height at most one the conclusion is the hypothesis taken at P' = P.
check.note: No Noetherian hypothesis is placed on R itself, which costs nothing because only the regular local ring R_P and the primes inside P enter, and the hypothesis at P' = 0 supplies the generic étaleness that purity needs.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.existsUnique_torsion_lift
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, category theory, ring theory, homological algebra, combinatorics

a.states: Let W be a local ring that is complete for its maximal ideal, with residue field k, let S be a scheme, G a smooth commutative group scheme over S, p a morphism from Spec W to S, and N a natural number that is a unit in W. For every k-point x₀ of G over the composite Spec k → Spec W → S with x₀^N = 1 there is exactly one W-point x of G over p with x^N = 1 whose restriction to Spec k is x₀.
a.notation: G/S smooth commutative group scheme, W complete local with residue field k, N ∈ W^×, x₀ ∈ G(k), x₀^N = 1 ⟹ ∃! x ∈ G(W) with x^N = 1 and x|_{Spec k} = x₀
a.known_as: unique lifting of N-torsion points from the residue field to a henselian local ring, that is the bijectivity of G[N](W) → G[N](k) for the étale group scheme G[N] when N is invertible
a.reference: S. Bosch, W. Lütkebohmert and M. Raynaud, Néron Models, 1990
a.why: A complete local ring is henselian and G[N] is étale over W when N is invertible, so the statement is the henselian lifting property of étale schemes in this case, though I know no single textbook statement phrased for torsion of smooth group schemes.

b.states: Let W be a local ring that is complete and separated for its maximal ideal, S a scheme, G a commutative group object over S with smooth structure morphism, p a morphism from Spec W to S, and N a natural number that is a unit in W. For every morphism x₀ over S from the spectrum of the residue field of W to G with x₀^N = 1, there is exactly one morphism x over S from Spec W to G such that x^N = 1 and the composite of Spec of the residue map with x equals x₀.
b.known_as: bijectivity of reduction on N-torsion points over a henselian local ring when N is invertible, from the étaleness of the N-torsion and Hensel's lemma (EGA IV §18.5)

check.known_as: bijectivity of reduction on N-torsion points over a henselian local ring when N is invertible, from the étaleness of the N-torsion subgroup scheme and Hensel's lemma (EGA IV 18.5)
check.note: Existence of the lift uses that a complete local ring is henselian, and its uniqueness holds over any local ring in which N is invertible, as in Theorem 44.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.uniform_serre_vanishing_cech_cocycles
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let R be a Noetherian ring, I an ideal of R, and J_e for e ∈ ℕ ideals of S = R[X_0,…,X_n] such that for every a ∈ I and every homogeneous form F ∈ J_e whose coefficients lie in I^e the product aF lies in J_{e+1}. Then there is d₀ such that for all d ≥ d₀, all e and all N, every family of forms F_{ij} of degree d + 2N with coefficients in I^e for which X_l^N F_{ij} + X_i^N F_{jl} − X_j^N F_{il} lies in J_e after multiplication by a power of X_iX_jX_l is a Čech coboundary with coefficients in I^e. That means there are N' and forms G_i of degree d + N' with coefficients in I^e such that (X_iX_j)^{N'}F_{ij} − (X_iX_j)^N(X_j^{N'}G_i − X_i^{N'}G_j) lies in J_e after multiplication by a power of X_iX_j.
a.notation: ∃ d₀ ∀ d ≥ d₀ ∀ e ∀ N, every Čech 1-cocycle (F_{ij}/(X_iX_j)^N) of (S/J_e)~(d) with F_{ij} ∈ I^e·S_{d+2N} is the coboundary of some (G_i/X_i^{N'}) with G_i ∈ I^e·S_{d+N'}
a.known_as: Serre's vanishing theorem for the first cohomology of twisted coherent sheaves on projective space, applied over the Rees algebra R[It] so that the bound d₀ is uniform along the I-adic filtration
a.reference: J.-P. Serre, Faisceaux algébriques cohérents, Annals of Mathematics 61 (1955)
a.why: The hypothesis on J makes the direct sum over e of I^e·S modulo J_e a finitely generated graded module over the Noetherian ring R[It][X_0,…,X_n], and Serre vanishing for H¹ of its sheaf on projective space over Spec R[It] gives the statement in each degree e, but this reading is mine and no published text states the result in this form.

b.states: For a Noetherian ring R, an ideal I of R, a natural number n and a family J of ideals of R[X_0,…,X_n] indexed by e, the statement assumes that aF lies in J(e+1) whenever a lies in I, F is homogeneous with all coefficients in I^e and F lies in J e. Then there is d₀ with the following property for all d ≥ d₀, all e and all N. Let the forms F_{ij} have degree d + 2N and coefficients in I^e, and let the fractions F_{ij}/(X_iX_j)^N satisfy the Čech cocycle identity modulo J e after multiplication by a power of X_iX_jX_l. Then there are N' and forms G_i of degree d + N' with coefficients in I^e such that F_{ij}/(X_iX_j)^N equals G_i/X_i^{N'} − G_j/X_j^{N'} modulo J e after multiplication by a power of X_iX_j.
b.known_as: Serre's vanishing theorem for H¹ of twists, applied over the Rees algebra of I so that the bound is uniform in e, written with Čech cocycles for the standard affine cover of projective n-space

check.known_as: Serre's vanishing theorem for H¹ of twisted coherent sheaves on projective space, applied over the Rees algebra of I so that the bound d₀ is uniform in e and written with Čech cocycles of the standard affine cover
check.note: The ideals J e are not assumed homogeneous, which costs nothing because every element that the statement tests for membership in some J e is homogeneous.

theorems.name: Formalism.MainNotions.LiftingTheory.desc_sub
theorems.areas: p-adic numbers

a.states: Let ℓ be a prime and O a commutative ℤ_ℓ-algebra, and let H₁, H₂, H₁', H₂' be O-modules with submodules Hf₁, Hf₂, Hf₁', Hf₂' and with O-linear maps h from H₁ to H₂, h' from H₁' to H₂', res₂ from H₂' to H₂, cor₁ from H₁ to H₁' and cor₂ from H₂ to H₂'. Assume that g > 0, cor₂ ∘ res₂ is multiplication by g, h' ∘ cor₁ = cor₂ ∘ h, res₂ maps Hf₂' into Hf₂, cor₁ maps Hf₁ into Hf₁', and every κ ∈ Hf₂ satisfies ℓ^E·κ = h(κ₁) for some κ₁ ∈ Hf₁. Then every κ' ∈ Hf₂' satisfies ℓ^{E + v_ℓ(g)}·κ' = h'(κ₁') for some κ₁' ∈ Hf₁', where v_ℓ is the ℓ-adic valuation.
a.notation: cor₂∘res₂ = g, h'∘cor₁ = cor₂∘h, res₂(Hf₂') ⊆ Hf₂, cor₁(Hf₁) ⊆ Hf₁', ℓ^E·Hf₂ ⊆ h(Hf₁) ⟹ ℓ^{E+v_ℓ(g)}·Hf₂' ⊆ h'(Hf₁')
a.known_as: no published result known, an elementary restriction and corestriction lemma for modules over a ℤ_ℓ-algebra
a.why: The proof applies the hypothesis to res₂(κ'), pushes the result forward with cor₁ and divides by the ℓ-adic unit g/ℓ^{v_ℓ(g)}, so the statement is a short bookkeeping lemma and not a result of the literature.

b.states: Let ℓ be a prime and O a commutative ℤ_ℓ-algebra, with O-modules H₁, H₂, H₁', H₂', submodules Hf₁, Hf₂, Hf₁', Hf₂', linear maps h from H₁ to H₂, h' from H₁' to H₂', res₂ from H₂' to H₂, cor₁ from H₁ to H₁' and cor₂ from H₂ to H₂', and natural numbers g > 0 and E. Assume that cor₂(res₂ x) = g·x and h'(cor₁ x) = cor₂(h x) for all x, that res₂ maps Hf₂' into Hf₂ and cor₁ maps Hf₁ into Hf₁', and that every κ in Hf₂ has some κ₁ in Hf₁ with h κ₁ = ℓ^E·κ. Then every κ' in Hf₂' has some κ₁' in Hf₁' with h' κ₁' = ℓ^(E + v_ℓ(g))·κ', where v_ℓ(g) is the ℓ-adic valuation of g.
b.known_as: no published result known
b.vacuity: None found, though the conclusion follows in a few lines by applying the last hypothesis to res₂ κ', pushing the result through cor₁ and dividing by the part of g prime to ℓ, which is a unit in ℤ_ℓ.

check.known_as: no published result known, an elementary restriction and corestriction lemma for modules over a ℤ_ℓ-algebra
check.note: The proof applies the last hypothesis to res₂ κ', pushes the result through cor₁ and divides by the part of g prime to ℓ, which is invertible in O because it is a unit of ℤ_ℓ.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.ChevalleySUnits.exists_places
theorems.areas: number fields, ring theory

a.states: Let E be a number field, S a finite set of nonzero primes of its ring of integers and m a positive integer. Then there is a finite set T of nonzero primes, disjoint from S, such that every x ∈ E^× that is a unit at every prime outside S and satisfies x ≡ 1 modulo every t ∈ T is an m-th power of an element of E.
a.notation: ∃ T finite with T ∩ S = ∅ such that ∀ x ∈ O_{E,S}^×, (x ≡ 1 mod t for all t ∈ T) ⟹ x ∈ (E^×)^m
a.known_as: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup of finite index in a finitely generated subgroup of the multiplicative group of a number field contains a congruence subgroup, here for the S-unit group and its subgroup of m-th powers
a.reference: C. Chevalley, Deux théorèmes d'arithmétique, Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan 3 (1951)
a.why: An m-th root in E of an S-unit is again an S-unit, and the squarefree modulus prime to S follows from a Chevalley modulus prime to S and to m by raising x to a power prime to m, but I am not certain which form of the modulus the published statement gives.

b.states: For a number field E, a finite set S of maximal ideals of its ring of integers and a natural number m > 0, there is a finite set T of maximal ideals disjoint from S with the following property. Every nonzero x in E whose valuation is trivial at every prime outside S, and for which x − 1 has valuation less than 1 at every prime in T, is the m-th power of an element of E.
b.known_as: Chevalley's theorem on S-units, that for every m some modulus makes each S-unit congruent to 1 modulo it an m-th power, where the Lean form also asks for a modulus made of distinct primes outside S

check.known_as: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup of finite index in the S-unit group of a number field contains a congruence subgroup, here for the subgroup of m-th powers
check.note: The Lean form asks for a modulus made of distinct primes outside S, which the usual statement does not mention but which follows from a Chevalley modulus prime to S and to m by raising x to a power prime to m.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.PurityProd.etale_integralClosure_of_isArtinianRing
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, group theory

a.states: Let A be a regular local ring and E a reduced Artinian A-algebra on which nonzero elements of A act injectively, and assume that the integral closure B of A in E is a finite A-module. If B ⊗_A A_q is étale over A_q for every prime q of A of height at most one, then B is étale over A.
a.notation: A regular local, E reduced Artinian and torsion-free over A, B = integral closure of A in E finite over A, B_q étale over A_q for all primes q with ht q ≤ 1 ⟹ B étale over A
a.known_as: the Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus
a.reference: M. Nagata, On the purity of branch loci in regular local rings, Illinois Journal of Mathematics 3 (1959)
a.vacuity: When dim A ≤ 1 the maximal ideal has height at most one and the conclusion is the hypothesis at that ideal, and for dim A ≥ 2 none found.
a.why: Torsion-freeness makes the product of fields E an algebra over the fraction field K of A, the hypothesis at q = 0 makes B ⊗ K finite étale over K, and B is then the integral closure of A in that finite étale algebra, which is the setting of purity of the branch locus.

b.states: For a regular local ring A and an A-algebra E that is reduced, Artinian and torsion-free over A, the statement assumes that the integral closure B of A in E is a finite A-module. It also assumes that A_q ⊗_A B is étale over A_q for every prime q of A of height at most 1. Under these hypotheses B is étale over A.
b.known_as: Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus for a finite normal algebra over a regular local ring
b.vacuity: When A has dimension at most 1 its maximal ideal has height at most 1, so the conclusion is the hypothesis at the maximal ideal up to the isomorphism of A with its localization there, but in higher dimension the statement has content.

check.known_as: Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus
check.vacuity: None found, although when A has dimension at most one the conclusion is the hypothesis at the maximal ideal up to the isomorphism of A with its localization there.
check.note: Torsion-freeness makes the reduced Artinian ring E an algebra over the fraction field K of A, and the hypothesis at q = 0 makes the integral closure tensored with K a finite étale K-algebra, which is the setting of purity.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_homogeneous_form_of_compatible_fractions
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let A be a Noetherian ring and J a homogeneous ideal of S = A[X_0,…,X_n]. Then there is d₀ such that for every d ≥ d₀ and every N, every family of forms F_i of degree d + N for which X_j^N F_i − X_i^N F_j lies in J after multiplication by a power of X_iX_j comes from a single form G of degree d. That means X_i^L(F_i − X_i^N G) lies in J for some L, for every i, so the fractions F_i/X_i^N all equal G in the localizations of S/J.
a.notation: ∃ d₀ ∀ d ≥ d₀, the map (S/J)_d → Γ(P^n_A, (S/J)~(d)) is surjective, with a global section written as fractions F_i/X_i^N, deg F_i = d + N, that agree on D(X_iX_j)
a.known_as: the fact that the natural map M_d → Γ(P^n, M~(d)) is an isomorphism for d large, here its surjectivity for M = S/J
a.reference: R. Hartshorne, Algebraic Geometry, 1977
a.why: The Lean conclusion is surjectivity onto global sections written in the standard affine cover, and Exercise II.5.9 in Hartshorne gives the isomorphism in large degrees for every finitely generated graded module.

b.states: For a Noetherian ring A, a natural number n and an ideal J of A[X_0,…,X_n] that contains every homogeneous component of each of its elements, there is d₀ with the following property for all d ≥ d₀ and all N. Let the forms F_i have degree d + N, and let the fractions F_i/X_i^N agree modulo J on each overlap after multiplication by a power of X_iX_j. Then there is a form G of degree d such that, for every i, F_i/X_i^N equals G modulo J after multiplication by a power of X_i.
b.known_as: the theorem that M_d → H⁰(Pⁿ, M~(d)) is an isomorphism for d large when M is a finitely generated graded module (Serre, FAC, and Hartshorne Exercise II.5.9), here its surjectivity for M = A[X]/J

check.known_as: the theorem that M_d → Γ(Pⁿ, M~(d)) is an isomorphism for large d when M is a finitely generated graded module (Hartshorne, Exercise II.5.9), here its surjectivity for M = A[X_0,…,X_n]/J
check.note: The homogeneity hypothesis on J costs nothing, because every element that the statement tests for membership in J is homogeneous.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.ChevalleyUnitsProof.core
theorems.areas: number fields

a.states: Let E be a number field, l a prime, r a natural number and b a positive integer. Then there is a positive integer a coprime to b such that every unit u of the ring of integers of E with u − 1 divisible by a is the l^r-th power of a unit.
a.notation: ∃ a ∈ ℕ, a > 0, gcd(a, b) = 1, ∀ u ∈ O_E^×, u ≡ 1 (mod a·O_E) ⟹ ∃ v ∈ O_E^×, u = v^{l^r}
a.known_as: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup of finite index in the unit group of a number field contains a congruence subgroup, here for the subgroup of l^r-th powers with a modulus prime to b
a.reference: C. Chevalley, Deux théorèmes d'arithmétique, Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan 3 (1951)
a.why: The statement is Chevalley's theorem for prime-power exponents with a rational modulus, and a modulus prime to b is what the Chebotarev proof gives, but I am not certain that the published statement includes the coprimality clause.

b.states: For a number field E, a prime l and natural numbers r and b with b > 0, there is a natural number a > 0 coprime to b such that every unit u of the ring of integers of E with a dividing u − 1 equals v^(l^r) for some unit v.
b.known_as: Chevalley's theorem on units, that for every m some integer modulus makes each unit congruent to 1 modulo it an m-th power, where the Lean form also asks for a modulus coprime to a given b

check.known_as: Chevalley's theorem on units of a number field, that for every exponent n some integer modulus makes each unit congruent to 1 an n-th power of a unit, here for prime-power exponents and a modulus prime to a given b
check.note: The coprimality of the modulus with b is more than the usual statement on units asserts, but it follows from the S-unit form of Chevalley's theorem with S the primes dividing b, and the restriction to exponents l^r loses nothing because the statement covers every prime l and every r.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.mem_span_sup_pow_of_forall_complete_dvr_local_test
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let O be a local normal domain of characteristic zero that is essentially of finite type over ℤ, with maximal ideal 𝔪, let g ∈ O be nonzero, and let (b_n) be a sequence in O with b_m − b_n ∈ 𝔪^m whenever m ≤ n. Assume that for every complete discrete valuation ring V of characteristic zero and every injective local homomorphism ρ from O to V one has ρ(b_e) ∈ ρ(g)V + 𝔪_V^e for every e. Then b_n ∈ gO + 𝔪^n for every n. In other words, the limit of (b_n) in the completion of O lies in the principal ideal generated by g as soon as its image does under every such map.
a.notation: (b_n) 𝔪-adically Cauchy, and for all complete DVRs V of characteristic 0 and all injective local ρ ∈ Hom(O, V), ρ(b_e) ∈ (ρ(g)) + 𝔪_V^e for all e ⟹ b_n ∈ (g) + 𝔪^n for all n
a.known_as: a test of membership in a principal ideal of the completion by maps into complete discrete valuation rings, akin to the valuative criterion for integral closure of ideals applied to the analytically normal completion of an excellent normal local domain
a.reference: I. Swanson and C. Huneke, Integral Closure of Ideals, Rings, and Modules, 2006
a.why: The statement is clearly shaped for one use, but the published valuative criterion tests all discrete valuations and does not restrict to injective local maps into complete rings of characteristic zero, so the link to the literature is one of method only.

b.states: Let O be an integrally closed local domain of characteristic zero that is essentially of finite type over ℤ, g a nonzero element of O and b a sequence in O with b_m − b_n in 𝔪^m whenever m ≤ n, where 𝔪 is the maximal ideal. Assume that ρ(b_e) lies in ρ(g)V + 𝔪_V^e for every complete discrete valuation ring V of characteristic zero, every injective local ring homomorphism ρ from O to V and every e. Then b_n lies in gO + 𝔪^n for every n.
b.known_as: no published result known

check.known_as: no published result known, a valuative test of membership in a principal ideal of the completion of an excellent normal local domain
check.note: The statement says that the limit of the Cauchy sequence b in the completion of O lies in g times the completion whenever every complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero that dominates O sees this, and it rests on the completion being a normal domain because O is excellent.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.ChevalleySUnits.exists_places_of_fg
theorems.areas: number fields, ring theory, group theory

a.states: Let E be a number field, Γ a finitely generated subgroup of E^×, S a finite set of nonzero primes of the ring of integers of E and m a positive integer. Then there is a finite set T of nonzero primes, disjoint from S, such that every x ∈ Γ with x ≡ 1 modulo every t ∈ T is an m-th power of an element of E.
a.notation: Γ ≤ E^× finitely generated ⟹ ∃ T finite with T ∩ S = ∅ such that ∀ x ∈ Γ, (x ≡ 1 mod t for all t ∈ T) ⟹ x ∈ (E^×)^m
a.known_as: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup of finite index in a finitely generated subgroup of the multiplicative group of a number field contains a congruence subgroup
a.reference: C. Chevalley, Deux théorèmes d'arithmétique, Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan 3 (1951)
a.why: Chevalley's theorem gives x ∈ Γ^m while the Lean statement concludes only that x is an m-th power in E, and its squarefree modulus prime to S follows from a modulus prime to S and to m by raising x to a power prime to m, though the exact published form of the modulus is not certain to me.

b.states: For a number field E, a finitely generated subgroup Γ of E^×, a finite set S of maximal ideals of the ring of integers and a natural number m > 0, there is a finite set T of maximal ideals disjoint from S with the following property. Every x in Γ for which x − 1 has valuation less than 1 at every prime in T is the m-th power of an element of E.
b.known_as: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup of finite index in a finitely generated subgroup of E^× contains a congruence subgroup, applied to Γ ∩ E^{×m}, where the Lean form also asks for a modulus made of distinct primes outside S

check.known_as: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup of finite index in a finitely generated subgroup Γ of E^× contains a congruence subgroup
check.note: The conclusion asks only for an m-th root in E and not in Γ, and the modulus made of distinct primes outside S follows from a Chevalley modulus prime to S and to m by raising x to a power prime to m.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.ChevalleySUnits.core

Then there is a finite set T of nonzero primes, disjoint from S, such that every x ∈ Γ with x ≡ 1 modulo every t ∈ T is an l^r-th power of an element of E.
a.notation: Γ ≤ E^× finitely generated, l prime ⟹ ∃ T finite with T ∩ S = ∅ such that ∀ x ∈ Γ, (x ≡ 1 mod t for all t ∈ T) ⟹ x ∈ (E^×)^{l^r}
a.known_as: Chevalley's theorem that every subgroup of finite index in a finitely generated subgroup of the multiplicative group of a number field contains a congruence subgroup, here for the exponent l^r
a.reference: C. Chevalley, Deux théorèmes d'arithmétique, Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan 3 (1951)
a.why: The statement is Theorem 54 for the exponent l^r, the prime-power case to which a general exponent reduces, and it follows from Chevalley's theorem in the same way with the same uncertainty about the form of the modulus.

b.states: For a number field E, a finitely generated subgroup Γ of E^×, a finite set S of maximal ideals of the ring of integers, a prime l and a natural number r, there is a finite set T of maximal ideals disjoint from S with the following property. b.known_as: Chevalley's theorem on congruence subgroups of a finitely generated subgroup of E^×, for the exponent l^r, where the Lean form also asks for a modulus made of distinct primes outside S

check.known_as: Chevalley's theorem on congruence subgroups of a finitely generated subgroup of E^×, for the exponent l^r
