a.why: On each fibre the smooth connected X_s is irreducible of dimension g′ and contains the nonempty closed Y_s of dimension g ≥ g′, so Y_s = X_s, and the fibrewise isomorphism criterion of EGA IV 17.9.5 then gives the claim, but I know no textbook that states this combination as a lemma.

b.states: Let S, X and Y be schemes, let p be a morphism from X to S and let f be a closed immersion from Y to X. Suppose p is geometrically connected, the composite f ≫ p is surjective, p is smooth of relative dimension g', f ≫ p is smooth of relative dimension g, and g' ≤ g. Then f is an isomorphism.
b.known_as: fibrewise criterion for a morphism of flat, locally finitely presented S-schemes to be an isomorphism (EGA IV 17.9.5), here reached after a dimension count on the connected smooth fibres
b.vacuity: None found, although the hypotheses force g = g', because a closed subscheme of a fibre of p cannot have larger dimension than that fibre.

check.known_as: no published result known, a fibrewise dimension criterion for a closed immersion between smooth S-schemes to be an isomorphism
check.vacuity: None found, although the hypotheses force g = g′, because a nonempty closed subscheme of the irreducible fibre X_s cannot have larger dimension than X_s.
check.note: The proof needs that each fibre X_s is irreducible, which holds because a smooth connected scheme over a field is irreducible, and that Y is flat over S, which lets the fibrewise isomorphism criterion of EGA IV 17.9.5 apply.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_dirichletLFunction_zero_gap_near_one
theorems.areas: zeta and L-series, Dirichlet and multiplicative characters, special functions

a.states: There is a constant c > 0 with the following property. For every modulus q ≥ 1, every complex Dirichlet character χ modulo q, and every complex zero ρ of the Dirichlet L-function L(s, χ) with |Im ρ| ≤ 1, one has 1 − Re ρ ≥ c/(q² log(3q)). The point ρ = 1 is excluded when χ is trivial.
a.notation: ∃ c > 0 ∀ q ≥ 1 ∀ χ mod q ∀ ρ ∈ ℂ, (χ ≠ 1 ∨ ρ ≠ 1), L(ρ, χ) = 0, |Im ρ| ≤ 1 ⟹ 1 − Re ρ ≥ c/(q² log 3q)
a.known_as: the classical zero-free region of de la Vallée Poussin for Dirichlet L-functions together with the effective bound 1 − β ≫ q^{−1/2}(log q)^{−2} for a possible exceptional real zero β
a.reference: Harold Davenport, Multiplicative Number Theory, 2nd edition, 1980, Chapter 14
a.vacuity: None found, and the condition χ ≠ 1 or ρ ≠ 1 only removes the pole of the L-function of the trivial character at s = 1, where Mathlib assigns a finite value.
a.why: The classical bounds, c/log(3q) for ordinary zeros and c/(q^{1/2} log² q) for an exceptional zero, both exceed a constant times 1/(q² log 3q), so the Lean statement follows and claims much less, and its crude shape with q² and |Im ρ| ≤ 1 points to a bound tailored for one later use.

b.states: There is a real number c > 0 with the following property. For every natural number q ≥ 1, every complex Dirichlet character χ modulo q and every complex number ρ with χ ≠ 1 or ρ ≠ 1, if L(χ, ρ) = 0 and |Im ρ| ≤ 1, then c/(q²·log(3q)) ≤ 1 − Re ρ.
b.known_as: zero-free region for Dirichlet L-functions near s = 1 (de la Vallée Poussin, Landau, Page) together with the effective bound 1 − β ≫ q^(−1/2)(log q)^(−2) for a possible exceptional real zero
b.vacuity: None found, and the excluded case χ = 1 with ρ = 1 only removes the pole of the trivial character at s = 1, where the Lean L-function carries a conventional value.

check.known_as: the zero-free region of de la Vallée Poussin for Dirichlet L-functions together with the effective bound 1 − β ≫ q^{−1/2}(log q)^{−2} for a possible exceptional real zero
check.note: The factor q² makes the bound much weaker than the classical bounds c/log(3q) for ordinary zeros and c/(q^{1/2} log² q) for an exceptional zero, and the trivial zeros and the zeros of imprimitive characters on Re s = 0 meet it at once.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.SmoothDedekind.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension_of_localization
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, field theory, group theory

a.states: Let o be a Noetherian ring and V a discrete valuation ring that is the localization of o at a submonoid M, with perfect residue field k and fraction field K. Let A be a flat o-algebra of finite type, and let d be a natural number such that every irreducible component of the generic fibre K ⊗_o A has Krull dimension at least d. Let x be a maximal ideal of the special fibre k ⊗_o A whose cotangent space x/x² has dimension at most d over the residue field. Then some f ∈ A outside the preimage of x in A makes the localization A_f a standard smooth o-algebra of relative dimension d.
a.notation: V = M⁻¹o DVR, k perfect, A flat f.t. over o, dim (K ⊗_o A)/𝔭 ≥ d ∀ minimal 𝔭, x ∈ Max(k ⊗_o A), dim_{κ(x)} x/x² ≤ d ⟹ ∃ f ∉ x ∩ A, A_f standard smooth of rel. dim d over o
a.known_as: the fibrewise criterion for smoothness of a flat morphism of finite presentation, applied at a closed point of the special fibre over a discrete valuation ring where that fibre is regular of the generic dimension and hence smooth over the perfect residue field
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck, Éléments de géométrie algébrique IV, quatrième partie, 1967, Théorème 17.5.1
a.why: Flatness over V makes every component of the special fibre through x have dimension at least d, and the bound on x/x² then makes that fibre regular, and so smooth, of dimension d at x, after which the fibrewise criterion gives smoothness of A near x, so the Lean statement follows from published results without being one of them.

b.states: Let o be a Noetherian ring, let V be a discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field that is the localization of o at a submonoid M, let K be the fraction field of V, and let A be a flat o-algebra of finite type. Suppose that dim((K ⊗_o A)/p) ≥ d for every minimal prime p of K ⊗_o A. Suppose further that x is a maximal ideal of the special fibre κ(V) ⊗_o A whose cotangent space x/x² has dimension at most d over the residue field. Then some f in A outside the preimage of x makes the localization A_f a standard smooth o-algebra of relative dimension d.
b.known_as: fibrewise criterion for smoothness, which says that a flat finitely presented algebra whose fibre is smooth at a point is smooth there (EGA IV 17.5.1), here combined with a tangent-space and fibre-dimension count on the special fibre
b.vacuity: None found, because the hypotheses hold for instance with o = ℤ, V = ℤ_(p), A = ℤ[t], d = 1 and x = (t) in 𝔽_p[t].

check.known_as: no published result known, a smoothness criterion at a closed point of the special fibre of a flat finite-type algebra over a discrete valuation ring, obtained from the fibrewise criterion of EGA IV 17.5.1 and a tangent-space dimension count
check.vacuity: None found, since the hypotheses hold for instance with o = ℤ, V = ℤ_(p), A = ℤ[t], d = 1 and x = (t) in 𝔽_p[t].
check.note: Because V is a localization of o, the fields K and ResidueField V are residue fields of points of Spec o, so K ⊗_o A and ResidueField V ⊗_o A are fibres of A over Spec o, and the conclusion asks for smoothness over o itself on a neighbourhood D(f) of the prime under x.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_conductor_adicCompletion_essFiniteType
theorems.areas: ring theory, group theory

a.states: Let A be an integrally closed local domain of characteristic zero that is essentially of finite type over ℤ, and let Â be its completion with respect to the maximal ideal. Then there is a nonzero x ∈ A such that x·c lies in Â for every element c of the total ring of fractions of Â that is integral over Â. In other words, the conductor of Â in its integral closure contains a nonzero element of A.
a.notation: A normal local domain, char 0, ess. f.t. over ℤ ⟹ ∃ x ∈ A∖{0} ∀ c ∈ Q(Â) integral over Â, x c ∈ Â
a.known_as: Zariski's theorem on analytic normality in Grothendieck's form, that the completion of an excellent normal local ring is normal, applied to a local ring essentially of finite type over ℤ, which is excellent
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck, Éléments de géométrie algébrique IV, seconde partie, 1965, Scholie 7.8.3
a.vacuity: None found, although x = 1 already satisfies the conclusion once Â is known to be a normal domain.
a.why: A is excellent and normal, so Â is a normal domain and every integral c already lies in Â, which means the Lean statement follows from the published theorem with a weaker conclusion that looks shaped for a proof needing only a nonzero conductor element.

b.states: Let A be a local, integrally closed domain of characteristic zero that is essentially of finite type over ℤ, and let Â be its completion at the maximal ideal. Then there is a nonzero x in A with the following property. For every element c of the total ring of fractions of Â that is integral over Â, the product x·c lies in the image of Â. In other words, x lies in the conductor of Â in its integral closure.
b.known_as: analytic normality of excellent normal local rings, which says that the completion of a normal local ring essentially of finite type over ℤ is normal (Zariski, EGA IV 7.8.3)
b.vacuity: No hypothesis is impossible to meet, but once one knows that Â is a normal domain the conclusion holds with x = 1, and the characteristic-zero hypothesis is not needed.

check.known_as: Zariski's analytic normality theorem in Grothendieck's form, that the completion of an excellent normal local ring is normal, applied to a local ring essentially of finite type over ℤ
check.vacuity: None found, although x = 1 meets the conclusion once one knows that Â is a normal domain, which is the deep content of the statement.
check.note: The characteristic-zero hypothesis plays no role in the published theorem, because every local ring essentially of finite type over ℤ is excellent.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_pow_eq_unit_of_continuous_complex_root
theorems.areas: complex analysis, other analysis, topology, ring theory

a.states: Let B be a smooth ℂ-algebra that is a domain, let n > 0, let u be a unit of B, and let ρ be a complex-valued function on the ℂ-algebra homomorphisms B → ℂ, which are the complex points of X = Spec B. Suppose that p ↦ ρ(s(p)) is continuous on V for every open V ⊆ ℂ^m and every map s from ℂ^m to these points whose coordinates p ↦ s(p)(a) are holomorphic on V. Suppose also that ρ(ψ)^n = ψ(u) for every point ψ. Then there is b ∈ B with b^n = u.
a.notation: B smooth ℂ-domain, n > 0, u ∈ B^×, ρ: X(ℂ) → ℂ continuous along holomorphic families, ρ^n = u on X(ℂ) ⟹ ∃ b ∈ B, b^n = u
a.known_as: the Riemann existence theorem in its fully faithful part, which makes continuous sections of the Kummer covering T^n = u over X(ℂ) algebraic, or equivalently the injectivity of B^×/(B^×)^n into H^1(X(ℂ), ℤ/n)
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck, Revêtements étales et groupe fondamental (SGA 1), 1971, Exposé XII, Théorème 5.1
a.vacuity: None found, and the continuity hypothesis is equivalent to ordinary continuity on the complex manifold X(ℂ), because X is smooth and has holomorphic charts.
a.why: A continuous n-th root of u is a continuous section of the finite étale covering Spec B[T]/(T^n − u) → X, and the Riemann existence theorem makes that section algebraic, so the Lean statement follows from the published theorem for one particular covering and is phrased for one use.

b.states: Let B be a domain that is a smooth ℂ-algebra, let n > 0, let u be a unit of B, and let ρ be a function from the ℂ-algebra maps B → ℂ to ℂ. Suppose ρ is continuous along holomorphic families, which means the following. For every m, every open V in ℂ^m and every map s from ℂ^m to the points whose coordinates a ∘ s are holomorphic on V, the function ρ ∘ s is continuous on V. If moreover ρ(ψ)^n = ψ(u) for every point ψ, then some b in B satisfies b^n = u, so a continuous n-th root of a unit on a smooth irreducible complex affine variety yields an algebraic one.
b.known_as: no published result known
b.vacuity: None found, because the hypotheses hold for instance with B = ℂ[t, t⁻¹], u = t², n = 2 and ρ(ψ) = ψ(t).

check.known_as: a consequence of the Riemann existence theorem (SGA 1, Exposé XII) for the Kummer covering T^n = u, which says that a continuous n-th root of a unit on a connected smooth complex affine variety is algebraic
check.vacuity: None found, since the hypotheses hold for instance with B = ℂ[t, t⁻¹], n = 2, u = t² and ρ(ψ) = ψ(t).
check.note: Continuity of ρ along holomorphic families is equivalent to ordinary continuity on the complex manifold X(ℂ), because the local charts of the smooth variety are holomorphic families, and the proof then needs that X(ℂ) is connected and that a continuous section of the finite étale covering T^n = u is algebraic.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.isSmoothAt_of_flat_of_finrank_cotangent_le_of_surjective
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, field theory, group theory

a.states: Let V be a discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field and fraction field K, let A be a flat V-algebra of finite type, and let d be a natural number such that every irreducible component of K ⊗_V A has Krull dimension at least d. Let φ: A → B be a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel 𝔪_V A, so B is the special fibre, and let x be a maximal ideal of B whose cotangent space x/x² has dimension at most d over B/x. Then A is smooth over V at the prime φ⁻¹(x), and some f ∉ φ⁻¹(x) makes A_f a standard smooth V-algebra of relative dimension d. Moreover, the local ring B_x is regular of Krull dimension d, and x/x² has dimension exactly d.
a.notation: A flat f.t. over V, dim (K ⊗ A)/𝔭 ≥ d ∀ minimal 𝔭, B = A/𝔪_V A, x ∈ Max B, dim x/x² ≤ d ⟹ A smooth at φ⁻¹x, ∃ f ∉ φ⁻¹x with A_f std. smooth of rel. dim d, B_x regular, dim B_x = dim x/x² = d
a.known_as: the fibrewise criterion for smoothness of a flat morphism of finite presentation, applied at a closed point of the special fibre over a discrete valuation ring where that fibre is regular of the generic dimension and hence smooth over the perfect residue field
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck, Éléments de géométrie algébrique IV, quatrième partie, 1967, Théorème 17.5.1
a.why: Flatness gives d ≤ dim B_x, and the hypothesis gives dim B_x ≤ dim x/x² ≤ d, so B_x is regular of dimension d and smooth over the perfect residue field, and the fibrewise criterion then gives the smoothness of A, which means the statement packages published facts for one use.

b.states: Let V be a discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field and fraction field K, let A be a flat V-algebra of finite type, and let d be a natural number with dim((K ⊗_V A)/p) ≥ d for every minimal prime p of K ⊗_V A. Let φ be a surjective ring map from A onto B with kernel m_V·A, so that B is the special fibre. Let x be a maximal ideal of B for which x/x² has dimension at most d over B/x. Then A is smooth over V at the prime φ⁻¹(x), some f outside φ⁻¹(x) makes A_f standard smooth of relative dimension d over V, the local ring B_x is regular of Krull dimension d, and x/x² has dimension exactly d.
b.known_as: fibrewise criterion for smoothness, which says that a flat finitely presented algebra whose fibre is smooth at a point is smooth there (EGA IV 17.5.1), here combined with a tangent-space and fibre-dimension count on the special fibre
b.vacuity: None found, because the hypotheses hold for instance with V = ℤ_(p), A = V[t], B = 𝔽_p[t], d = 1 and x = (t).

check.known_as: no published result known, a smoothness criterion at a closed point of the special fibre of a flat finite-type algebra over a discrete valuation ring, obtained from the fibrewise criterion of EGA IV 17.5.1 and a tangent-space dimension count
check.vacuity: None found, since the hypotheses hold for instance with V = ℤ_(p), A = V[t], B = 𝔽_p[t], d = 1 and x = (t).
check.note: The statement does not follow from the fibrewise criterion alone, since it also needs that flatness makes the special fibre at least d-dimensional at x and that a regular closed point over a perfect field is a smooth point, and theorem 135 is the same statement for an arbitrary local ring S that localizes B at x.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.Global.Elliptic.weierstrassP_halfPeriods_ne
theorems.areas: special functions

a.states: For every period pair L, which is a basis ω₁, ω₂ of a lattice in ℂ, the Weierstrass function ℘ of that lattice takes three pairwise different values at the half-periods ω₁/2, ω₂/2 and (ω₁ + ω₂)/2.
a.notation: e₁ = ℘(ω₁/2), e₂ = ℘(ω₂/2), e₃ = ℘((ω₁ + ω₂)/2) ⟹ e₁ ≠ e₂, e₁ ≠ e₃, e₂ ≠ e₃
a.known_as: distinctness of the half-period values e₁, e₂, e₃ of the Weierstrass ℘-function
a.reference: Lars V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd edition, 1979, Chapter 7, Section 3.3
a.why: The textbook proof observes that ℘ − e_i has a double zero at ω_i/2 and, as an elliptic function of order 2, no other zero in a period parallelogram, so two equal values would give too many zeros, and the Lean statement is exactly this claim.

b.states: Let L be a period pair with periods ω₁ and ω₂. Then the three values ℘(ω₁/2), ℘(ω₂/2) and ℘((ω₁ + ω₂)/2) of the Weierstrass function of L are pairwise distinct.
b.known_as: the half-period values e₁, e₂ and e₃ of the Weierstrass ℘-function are distinct, which is equivalent to the discriminant g₂³ − 27g₃² being nonzero

check.known_as: the distinctness of the half-period values e₁, e₂, e₃ of the Weierstrass ℘-function
check.note: This statement is the first three conjuncts of theorem 136, and the half-periods are not lattice points, so Mathlib's value of ℘ at its poles plays no role.

theorems.name: PositivityTheory.Xgn.TightHopfOrder.exists_complete_normal
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let V be an integrally closed local domain of characteristic zero, and let p be a prime number that lies in the maximal ideal of V. Assume that V is p-adically complete and Hausdorff and that every element of the maximal ideal has a power in pV. Let R₀ be a Noetherian ring with a ring homomorphism f: R₀ → V, and let s be a finite subset of V. Then there are a Noetherian integrally closed local domain D that is complete for its maximal ideal, a ring homomorphism g: R₀ → D, and an injective local homomorphism h: D → V such that h∘g = f and s lies in the image of h.
a.notation: V normal local domain, char 0, p ∈ 𝔪_V, V p-adically complete, 𝔪_V ⊆ √(pV), f: R₀ → V, R₀ Noetherian, s ⊆ V finite ⟹ ∃ complete Noetherian normal local domain D, g: R₀ → D, local injective h: D → V, h∘g = f, s ⊆ h(D)
a.known_as: no published result known, an approximation statement that exhausts a p-adically complete normal local domain by complete Noetherian normal local subrings containing a given Noetherian image
a.vacuity: None found, and the hypotheses hold for instance for V = ℤ_p and for the ring of integers of ℂ_p.
a.why: The proof would complete the localization of R₀[X₁, …, X_n] at the preimage of the maximal ideal, map the completion to V, which is complete in the matching adic topology, and take the normalization of the image, which is finite by Nagata's theorem on complete local rings and lies in V because V is integrally closed, but I know no source that states this, and its shape fits one step of a larger proof.

b.states: Let V be a local, integrally closed domain of characteristic zero, and let p be a prime number lying in the maximal ideal of V. Suppose V is complete and separated in the p-adic topology and its maximal ideal lies in the radical of (p). Then for every Noetherian ring R₀ with a ring map f to V and every finite subset s of V there exist the following objects. There are a Noetherian, integrally closed, local domain D that is complete for its maximal ideal and ring maps g from R₀ to D and h from D to V, such that h is injective and local, h ∘ g = f, and every element of s lies in the image of h.
b.known_as: no published result known
b.vacuity: None found, because the hypotheses hold for instance with V = ℤ_p or the ring of integers of ℂ_p and R₀ = ℤ.

check.known_as: no published result known, an approximation of a p-adically complete normal local domain by complete Noetherian normal local subrings that contain a given Noetherian image and a given finite set
check.vacuity: None found, since the hypotheses hold for instance with V = ℤ_p and R₀ = ℤ.
check.note: A proof can complete a localization of a finitely generated R₀-algebra that maps onto s, take its image in V and normalize it, and the normalization stays finite by Nagata's theorem on complete local domains and stays inside V because V is integrally closed.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.isSmoothAt_of_flat_of_finrank_cotangentSpace_le
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, field theory, group theory

a.states: Let V be a discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field and fraction field K, and let A be a flat V-algebra of finite type whose generic fibre K ⊗_V A has all irreducible components of Krull dimension at least d. Let φ: A → B be a surjection with kernel 𝔪_V A, let x be a maximal ideal of B, and let S be a local ring that is a localization of B at x. Suppose that the cotangent space 𝔪_S/𝔪_S² has dimension at most d over the residue field of S. Then A is smooth over V at φ⁻¹(x), some f ∉ φ⁻¹(x) makes A_f standard smooth of relative dimension d over V, S is a regular local ring of Krull dimension d, and the cotangent space of S has dimension exactly d.
a.notation: A flat f.t. over V, dim (K ⊗ A)/𝔭 ≥ d ∀ minimal 𝔭, B = A/𝔪_V A, S = B_x, dim 𝔪_S/𝔪_S² ≤ d ⟹ A smooth at φ⁻¹x, ∃ f ∉ φ⁻¹x with A_f std. smooth of rel. dim d, S regular, dim S = dim 𝔪_S/𝔪_S² = d
a.known_as: the fibrewise criterion for smoothness of a flat morphism of finite presentation, applied at a closed point of the special fibre over a discrete valuation ring where that fibre is regular of the generic dimension and hence smooth over the perfect residue field
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck, Éléments de géométrie algébrique IV, quatrième partie, 1967, Théorème 17.5.1
a.why: The statement is Theorem 132 with the cotangent space of the special fibre at x read off from an arbitrary model S of the localization B_x, so it rests on the same published facts and serves the same use.

b.states: The setting is that of theorem 132. V is a discrete valuation ring with perfect residue field and fraction field K, A is a flat V-algebra of finite type whose generic fibre has every component of dimension at least d, φ maps A onto B with kernel m_V·A, and x is a maximal ideal of B. In addition, S is a local ring that is the localization of B at x, and the cotangent space of S has dimension at most d over the residue field of S. Then A is smooth over V at φ⁻¹(x), some f outside φ⁻¹(x) makes A_f standard smooth of relative dimension d over V, S is a regular local ring of Krull dimension d, and its cotangent space has dimension exactly d.
b.known_as: fibrewise criterion for smoothness, which says that a flat finitely presented algebra whose fibre is smooth at a point is smooth there (EGA IV 17.5.1), here combined with a tangent-space and fibre-dimension count on the special fibre
b.vacuity: None found, because the hypotheses hold for instance with V = ℤ_(p), A = V[t], B = 𝔽_p[t], d = 1, x = (t) and S the localization of 𝔽_p[t] at (t).

check.known_as: no published result known, a smoothness criterion at a closed point of the special fibre of a flat finite-type algebra over a discrete valuation ring, obtained from the fibrewise criterion of EGA IV 17.5.1 and a tangent-space dimension count
check.vacuity: None found, since the hypotheses hold for instance with V = ℤ_(p), A = V[t], B = 𝔽_p[t], d = 1, x = (t) and S the localization of 𝔽_p[t] at (t).
check.note: This is theorem 132 with the localization B_x replaced by any local ring S that is a localization of B at x, so the cotangent space of S takes the place of x/x².

theorems.name: GroundTheory.Global.Elliptic.halfPeriod_facts
theorems.areas: special functions

a.states: Let L be a period pair, and let e₁ = ℘(ω₁/2), e₂ = ℘(ω₂/2) and e₃ = ℘((ω₁ + ω₂)/2) be the values of its Weierstrass function at the half-periods. Then the three values are pairwise different, e₁ + e₂ + e₃ = 0, 4(e₁² + e₁e₂ + e₂²) = g₂, and g₃ = 4e₁³ − g₂e₁, where g₂ and g₃ are the Weierstrass invariants of the lattice.
a.notation: e₁, e₂, e₃ pairwise distinct, e₁ + e₂ + e₃ = 0, 4(e₁² + e₁e₂ + e₂²) = g₂, g₃ = 4e₁³ − g₂e₁
a.known_as: the factorization 4x³ − g₂x − g₃ = 4(x − e₁)(x − e₂)(x − e₃) with distinct roots at the half-period values
a.reference: Lars V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd edition, 1979, Chapter 7, Section 3.3
a.why: Comparing coefficients in the factorization gives e₁ + e₂ + e₃ = 0, then 4(e₁² + e₁e₂ + e₂²) = g₂ after substituting e₃ = −e₁ − e₂, and finally the root equation for e₁, and these facts together with distinctness give back 4e₁e₂e₃ = g₃, so they are equivalent to the classical factorization with distinct roots.

b.states: Let L be a period pair, and write e₁ = ℘(ω₁/2), e₂ = ℘(ω₂/2) and e₃ = ℘((ω₁ + ω₂)/2). Then e₁, e₂ and e₃ are pairwise distinct and e₁ + e₂ + e₃ = 0. Moreover 4·(e₁² + e₁·e₂ + e₂²) = g₂ and g₃ = 4·e₁³ − g₂·e₁.
b.known_as: the half-period values of the Weierstrass ℘-function are the three distinct roots of 4x³ − g₂x − g₃, and Vieta's formulas give the stated relations

check.known_as: the factorization 4x³ − g₂x − g₃ = 4(x − e₁)(x − e₂)(x − e₃) with distinct roots at the half-period values of ℘
check.note: The three relations e₁ + e₂ + e₃ = 0, 4(e₁² + e₁e₂ + e₂²) = g₂ and g₃ = 4e₁³ − g₂e₁ are together equivalent to the factorization, and the first three conjuncts repeat theorem 133.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.Ar.Flat.PoleDisc.disc_of_pole
theorems.areas: complex analysis, other analysis, topology, ring theory

a.states: Let R be a Noetherian integrally closed domain that is a finitely generated ℚ-algebra, with fraction field K, and let g, h, b ∈ R with h ≠ 0, b ≠ 0 and g/h ∉ R. Then there are a map ψ from ℂ to the set of ring homomorphisms R → ℂ and a real constant C such that z ↦ ψ(z)(a) is holomorphic on the open unit disc for every a ∈ R. Moreover, for every z ≠ 0 in that disc, ψ(z)(b) ≠ 0, ψ(z)(h) ≠ 0 and |ψ(z)(h)| ≤ C|z||ψ(z)(g)|.
a.notation: R normal f.g. ℚ-domain, h, b ≠ 0, g/h ∉ R ⟹ ∃ holomorphic ψ: 𝔻 → (Spec R)(ℂ), ∃ C, ∀ z ∈ 𝔻∖{0}, b(ψ(z)) ≠ 0, h(ψ(z)) ≠ 0, |h(ψ(z))| ≤ C|z||g(ψ(z))|
a.known_as: no published result known, a holomorphic-disc witness that a rational function which is not regular on a normal affine ℚ-variety has a pole, in the spirit of the Riemann extension theorem on normal complex spaces
a.vacuity: None found, and the hypotheses hold for R = ℚ[t], g = b = 1 and h = t.
a.why: A proof would take a height-one prime where g/h has negative valuation, which exists because a normal Noetherian domain is the intersection of its localizations at height-one primes, and then a disc crossing that divisor transversally at a general smooth point, but I know no source that states this disc form, and Theorem 125 is its smooth case.

b.states: Let R be a Noetherian, integrally closed domain that is a finitely generated ℚ-algebra, and let K be its fraction field. Let g, h and b be elements of R with h ≠ 0, b ≠ 0 and g/h not in R. Then there exist a family ψ of ring homomorphisms from R to ℂ, indexed by z in ℂ, and a real number C such that z ↦ ψ z a is holomorphic on the open unit disc for every a in R. Moreover, for every z ≠ 0 in that disc, ψ z b ≠ 0, ψ z h ≠ 0 and |ψ z h| ≤ C·|z|·|ψ z g|.
b.known_as: no published result known
b.vacuity: None found, because the hypotheses hold for instance with R = ℚ[t], g = 1, h = t and b = 1.

check.known_as: no published result known, a holomorphic disc that runs into the polar divisor of a rational function g/h which is not regular on a normal affine ℚ-variety
check.vacuity: None found, since the hypotheses hold for instance with R = ℚ[t], g = b = 1 and h = t.
check.note: Theorem 125 is the special case in which the ring is smooth over ℚ and sits in its fraction field, because a smooth finitely generated ℚ-domain is Noetherian and integrally closed.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.exists_entire_sub_one_mul_euler_exp_ne_zero_one
theorems.areas: number fields, complex analysis, special functions, other analysis, topology, ring theory

a.states: For every number field K there is an entire function Z: ℂ → ℂ with Z(1) ≠ 0 such that Z(s) = (s − 1)·exp(Σ_P −log(1 − N(P)^{−s})) for Re s > 1, where the sum runs over the nonzero prime ideals P of the ring of integers 𝓞_K. For Re s > 1 the exponential equals the Euler product ∏_P (1 − N(P)^{−s})^{−1} = ζ_K(s). The statement therefore says that (s − 1)ζ_K(s) extends to an entire function that does not vanish at s = 1.
a.notation: ∀ K number field ∃ Z entire, Z(1) ≠ 0, Z(s) = (s − 1) ∏_𝔭 (1 − N𝔭^{−s})^{−1} = (s − 1) ζ_K(s) for Re s > 1
a.known_as: Hecke's theorem that the Dedekind zeta function continues meromorphically to ℂ with a single simple pole at s = 1, whose residue is nonzero by the analytic class number formula
a.reference: Jürgen Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, 1999, Chapter VII, Corollary 5.11
a.why: The Lean statement keeps the continuation of (s − 1)ζ_K(s) and the nonvanishing of the residue but drops the functional equation and the value of the residue, so it follows from the published theorem and claims less.

b.states: Let K be a number field. Then there is an entire function Z with Z(1) ≠ 0 such that Z(s) = (s − 1)·exp(Σ_P −log(1 − 1·N(P)^(−s))) for every s with Re s > 1, where P runs over the maximal ideals of 𝓞_K. The exponential is the Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function. So the statement says that (s − 1)·ζ_K(s) extends to an entire function that is nonzero at s = 1.
b.known_as: Hecke's theorem on the analytic continuation of the Dedekind zeta function to a meromorphic function on ℂ with a single simple pole at s = 1, here without the functional equation and the residue formula
b.vacuity: None found, and the Lean sum over the primes equals the true sum because the series converges absolutely for Re s > 1.

check.known_as: Hecke's theorem that the Dedekind zeta function continues meromorphically to ℂ with a single simple pole at s = 1
check.note: For Re s > 1 the exponential of the sum of −log(1 − N(P)^{−s}) equals the Euler product of ζ_K(s), the factor 1 in front of N(P)^{−s} changes nothing, and the statement leaves out the functional equation and the value of the residue.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.Global.differentiable_discr_cpow_mul_gamma_inv
theorems.areas: number fields, complex analysis, special functions, other analysis, topology

a.states: Let K be a number field with discriminant d_K, r₁ real places and r₂ complex places. Then the function s ↦ |d_K|^{−s/2}·(Γ_ℝ(s)^{r₁} Γ_ℂ(s)^{r₂})^{−1} is complex differentiable on all of ℂ, where Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s). Mathlib sets Γ equal to 0 at its poles and inverts 0 to 0, so the expression agrees at every point with the entire function |d_K|^{−s/2}/(Γ_ℝ(s)^{r₁} Γ_ℂ(s)^{r₂}).
a.notation: s ↦ |d_K|^{−s/2} (Γ_ℝ(s)^{r₁} Γ_ℂ(s)^{r₂})^{−1} is entire
a.known_as: the fact that the reciprocal Gamma function 1/Γ is entire, applied to the archimedean factor of the completed Dedekind zeta function
a.reference: Lars V. Ahlfors, Complex Analysis, 3rd edition, 1979, Chapter 5, Section 2.4
a.vacuity: None found, although the conclusion follows almost at once from the entireness of 1/Γ and of s ↦ |d_K|^{−s/2}.
a.why: Products and powers of the entire functions 1/Γ(s/2), 1/Γ(s), π^{s/2}, (2π)^s and |d_K|^{−s/2} are entire, so the statement is a direct consequence of the published fact and serves the continuation of the Dedekind zeta function.

b.states: Let K be a number field with discriminant d_K, r₁ real places and r₂ complex places. Then the function s ↦ |d_K|^(−s/2)·(Γ_ℝ(s)^(r₁)·Γ_ℂ(s)^(r₂))⁻¹ is complex differentiable on all of ℂ. Here Γ_ℝ(s) = π^(−s/2)·Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2·(2π)^(−s)·Γ(s).
b.known_as: the reciprocal of the Gamma function is entire (Weierstrass), applied to the archimedean gamma factor of the Dedekind zeta function

check.known_as: the entireness of the reciprocal Gamma function 1/Γ, applied to the archimedean factor of the completed Dedekind zeta function
check.vacuity: None found, although the conclusion follows quickly from the entireness of 1/Γ and of s ↦ |d_K|^{−s/2}.
check.note: Mathlib gives Γ the value 0 at its poles and inverts 0 to 0, so the Lean expression agrees at every point with the entire function |d_K|^{−s/2}/(Γ_ℝ(s)^{r₁}Γ_ℂ(s)^{r₂}).

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.formalFibre_isRegularRing_essFiniteType_int
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let R be a local ring essentially of finite type over ℤ, with maximal ideal 𝔪 and 𝔪-adic completion R̂, and let K be a field that is an R-algebra essentially of finite type over R. Then the ring R̂ ⊗_R K is regular. Let 𝔮 be the kernel of R → K. Then K is a finitely generated field extension of κ(𝔮) and R̂ ⊗_R K = (R̂ ⊗_R κ(𝔮)) ⊗_{κ(𝔮)} K, so the statement says that the formal fibres of R are geometrically regular.
a.notation: R local ess. f.t. over ℤ, K field ess. f.t. over R ⟹ R̂ ⊗_R K is regular
a.known_as: Grothendieck's theorem that rings essentially of finite type over ℤ are excellent, in its part that the formal fibres of such a local ring are geometrically regular
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck, Éléments de géométrie algébrique IV, seconde partie, 1965, Scholie 7.8.3
a.why: The Lean statement is equivalent to the G-ring condition for R, which is one of the three conditions that make up excellence, so it follows from Grothendieck's result and claims less, and textbooks such as Matsumura's Commutative Ring Theory state that result as a numbered theorem with no name.

b.states: Let R be a local ring essentially of finite type over ℤ, let R̂ be its completion at the maximal ideal, and let K be a field that is an R-algebra essentially of finite type over R. Then the ring R̂ ⊗_R K is a regular ring.
b.known_as: Grothendieck's theorem that rings essentially of finite type over ℤ are excellent, so the formal fibres of R are geometrically regular (EGA IV 7.8.3)

check.known_as: the excellence of rings essentially of finite type over ℤ (EGA IV 7.8.3), in its part that the formal fibres of such a local ring are geometrically regular
check.note: Because each such K is a finitely generated field extension of the residue field at the kernel of R → K, regularity of R̂ ⊗_R K for all such K is equivalent to geometric regularity of the formal fibres of R, which is the G-ring part of excellence.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.ThetaGauss.exists_zero_fderiv_ne_zero
theorems.areas: complex analysis, special functions, other analysis, topology, linear algebra

a.states: For every natural number g, every positive definite Hermitian matrix H in M_g(ℂ) and every discrete additive subgroup Λ of ℂ^g such that a vector v lies in Λ exactly when Im(v*Ha) is an integer for every a in Λ, the following holds for all functions χ and θ from ℂ^g to ℂ. If θ is holomorphic and not identically zero, |χ(a)| = 1 for every a in Λ, and θ(z + a) = χ(a)·exp(π·a*Hz + (π/2)·a*Ha)·θ(z) for every a in Λ and every z, then every nonzero vector v has a point a with θ(a) = 0 and dθ(a)(v) ≠ 0. The self-duality condition makes Λ a full lattice on which E = Im H is integral and unimodular, so θ is a theta function of a principal polarization on the torus ℂ^g/Λ. The conclusion says that no nonzero direction is tangent to the zero set of θ at every one of its zeros.
a.notation: ∀g ∀H ≻ 0 ∀Λ ≤ ℂ^g discrete with Λ = {v | Im(v*Ha) ∈ ℤ ∀a ∈ Λ}, ∀χ ∀θ entire, θ ≠ 0, |χ| = 1 on Λ, θ(z+a) = χ(a)e^{π a*Hz + (π/2) a*Ha}θ(z) ⟹ ∀v ≠ 0 ∃a, θ(a) = 0 ∧ dθ(a)v ≠ 0
a.known_as: Nondegeneracy of the Gauss map of the theta divisor of a principally polarized abelian variety. The tangent hyperplanes of a reduced ample divisor at its smooth points have no nonzero vector in common, and this is applied here to the reduced theta divisor.
a.reference: Christina Birkenhake and Herbert Lange, Complex Abelian Varieties, 2nd edition, 2004 (Section 4.4 on the Gauss map)
a.vacuity: For g = 0 the statement is empty because there is no nonzero vector, and for g ≥ 1 the Riemann theta function of a principally polarized abelian variety meets every hypothesis, so no other emptiness was found.
a.why: The content matches the link between ampleness and a nondegenerate Gauss image, combined with the reducedness of the theta divisor, but I recall the textbook wording only approximately, and the Lean text merges both facts in coordinates.

b.states: For every natural number g, every positive definite Hermitian g×g complex matrix H and every discrete additive subgroup Λ of ℂ^g, suppose Λ is exactly the set of vectors v for which Im(v* H a) is an integer for all a in Λ, where v* is the conjugate transpose. Suppose also that θ is a holomorphic function on ℂ^g that is not identically zero, and that χ is a function of modulus one on Λ with θ(z + a) = χ(a) exp(π a* H z + (π/2) a* H a) θ(z) for all a in Λ and all z. Then for every nonzero vector v there is a point a with θ(a) = 0 at which the directional derivative of θ in the direction v is nonzero.
b.known_as: Nondegeneracy of the theta divisor Θ of a principally polarized abelian variety, which says that Θ is not invariant under translation along any complex line. It follows from the finiteness of the translation stabilizer of an ample divisor (Mumford, Abelian Varieties, §6, Application 1) together with the reducedness of Θ
b.vacuity: None found, because a nonzero theta function exists for every principal polarization with a semicharacter χ, and only the case g = 0 makes the conclusion hold for lack of a nonzero v.

check.known_as: Nondegeneracy of the Gauss map of the theta divisor of a principally polarized abelian variety, which says that the tangent hyperplanes of the reduced theta divisor at its smooth points have no nonzero direction in common (Birkenhake and Lange, Complex Abelian Varieties, Section 4.4 on the Gauss map).
check.vacuity: The case g = 0 holds vacuously because ℂ^0 has no nonzero vector, and for every g ≥ 1 the Riemann theta function of a principal polarization meets all hypotheses, so no other emptiness was found.
check.note: The self-duality of Λ under Im H forces Λ to be a full lattice carrying a principal polarization, and the proof needs the reducedness of the theta divisor in addition to the ampleness of the polarization, since a zero of order two or more has a vanishing derivative in every direction.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.WeierstrassCurve.isReduced_coordinateRing
theorems.areas: algebraic geometry, ring theory

a.states: For every reduced commutative ring R and every Weierstrass curve W over R, the affine coordinate ring R[X, Y]/(Y² + a₁XY + a₃Y − X³ − a₂X² − a₄X − a₆) is a reduced ring. The declaration is an instance. Its displayed proof gets reducedness from two facts, that the coordinate ring is geometrically reduced over R, checked through pullback squares over every field, and that it is free as an R-module.
a.notation: R reduced ⟹ R[X,Y]/(Y² + a₁XY + a₃Y − X³ − a₂X² − a₄X − a₆) reduced
a.known_as: No published result known. It is a reducedness property of the coordinate ring of an affine Weierstrass curve over an arbitrary reduced base ring.
a.why: Over a field the matching integrality is textbook material, and the general case follows by a routine freeness argument, but I know no source that states the version over a reduced base, so the kind is a judgment.

b.states: For every commutative reduced ring R and every Weierstrass curve W over R, with no condition on the discriminant, the affine coordinate ring R[X, Y]/(Weierstrass polynomial of W) is a reduced ring. The statement is an instance declaration, so this reducedness is registered for automatic use.
b.known_as: Reducedness of the affine Weierstrass curve over a reduced base. It is an instance of the fact that an algebra that is free (flat) over a reduced ring and has geometrically reduced fibres is reduced, applied through the geometric integrality of Weierstrass cubics

check.known_as: No published result known. It is the reducedness of the affine coordinate ring of an arbitrary Weierstrass curve over a reduced base ring, which follows from the freeness of that ring over the base and the integrality of the Weierstrass cubic over every field.
check.note: The instance needs no condition on the discriminant, so it covers singular Weierstrass curves too, and the proof shown in the dossier goes through geometric reducedness over every field and freeness over R.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.Global.Elliptic.sub_mem_or_add_mem_of_weierstrassP_eq
theorems.areas: special functions

a.states: Let L be the lattice spanned by a pair of ℝ-linearly independent complex periods, and let ℘ be its Weierstrass function. For complex numbers z and w that both lie outside the lattice, ℘(z) = ℘(w) implies that z − w or z + w lies in the lattice.
a.notation: z, w ∉ L, ℘_L(z) = ℘_L(w) ⟹ z − w ∈ L ∨ z + w ∈ L
a.known_as: The Weierstrass ℘-function is an even elliptic function of order 2, so ℘(z) = ℘(w) holds exactly when z ≡ ±w modulo the lattice.
a.reference: Joseph H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 2nd edition, 2009 (Chapter VI)
a.why: The Lean text is the nontrivial direction of the classical description of the fibres of ℘, and the converse direction it leaves out follows at once from evenness and periodicity.

b.states: Let L be a period pair with lattice Λ, and let z and w be complex numbers that both lie outside Λ. If the Weierstrass function ℘ of L takes the same value at z and at w, then z − w or z + w lies in Λ.
b.known_as: One direction of the standard fact that ℘(z) = ℘(w) holds exactly when z ≡ ±w modulo the lattice, which holds because ℘ is an even elliptic function of order two

check.known_as: One direction of the description of the fibres of the Weierstrass function, which says that ℘(z) = ℘(w) holds exactly when z ≡ ±w modulo the lattice because ℘ is an even elliptic function of order 2.
check.note: The converse direction, that z ≡ ±w modulo the lattice gives ℘(z) = ℘(w), follows from evenness and periodicity and is not part of the statement.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.Global.Elliptic.two_mul_mem_lattice_iff_derivWeierstrassP_eq_zero
theorems.areas: special functions

a.states: Let L be a period lattice and w a complex number outside L. Then 2w lies in L if and only if the derivative ℘′ of the Weierstrass function of L vanishes at w.
a.known_as: The zeros of ℘′ are exactly the three nonzero half-periods modulo the lattice.
a.reference: Joseph H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, 2nd edition, 2009 (Chapter VI)
a.why: For points outside the lattice, the condition 2w ∈ L says exactly that w is a nonzero half-period, which is the classical description of the zeros of ℘′.

b.states: Let L be a period pair with lattice Λ and let w be a complex number outside Λ. Then 2w lies in Λ if and only if the derivative ℘′ of the Weierstrass function of L vanishes at w.
b.known_as: The zeros of ℘′ are exactly the three half periods modulo the lattice

check.known_as: The zeros of ℘′ are exactly the three nonzero half-periods modulo the lattice.
check.note: The point w has to lie outside the lattice because ℘′ has its poles at the lattice points, where 2w ∈ L holds trivially.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.GeomConn.isPreconnected_points_over
theorems.areas: other analysis, topology, ring theory

a.states: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, A a finitely generated commutative K-algebra, and Ω a field over K in which every element algebraic over K already lies in K. Let j be an injective K-algebra map from A to Ω and σ a ring embedding of K into ℂ. Then the set of ring homomorphisms ρ from A to ℂ with ρ restricted to K equal to σ is preconnected, viewed as a set of functions from A to ℂ with the product topology. Geometrically, Spec A is a geometrically integral affine K-variety, and the claim is that the complex points of its base change along σ form a connected space in the classical topology.
a.notation: {ρ ∈ Hom_ring(A, ℂ) | ρ ∘ (K → A) = σ} ⊆ ℂ^A is preconnected
a.known_as: An irreducible complex algebraic variety is connected in the classical topology.
a.reference: Igor R. Shafarevich, Basic Algebraic Geometry 2, 2nd edition, 1994 (Chapter VII, Section 2)
a.why: The hypotheses make A ⊗_{K,σ} ℂ a domain of finite type, so the set is the complex point set of an irreducible affine variety with its classical topology, and the Lean text is the affine case of the theorem, although calling that theorem a main theorem is a judgment.

b.states: Let K be a field of characteristic zero, A a finitely generated K-algebra and Ω a field over K in which every element algebraic over K already lies in K. Suppose there is an injective K-algebra homomorphism from A into Ω, and let σ be a ring homomorphism from K to ℂ. Then the set of ring homomorphisms from A to ℂ that restrict to σ on K is preconnected, where these homomorphisms are regarded as functions from A to ℂ with the product topology.
b.known_as: Connectedness in the classical topology of the complex points of an irreducible complex variety (Shafarevich, Basic Algebraic Geometry, Chapter VII, §2, and Mumford, Red Book, I §10). Here it is applied to the base change along σ of an affine variety over K, which is geometrically irreducible because K is algebraically closed in its function field
b.vacuity: None found, since A = K[x] inside Ω = K(x) meets the hypotheses and the set in the conclusion is nonempty in every case.

check.known_as: Connectedness of an irreducible complex algebraic variety in the classical topology (Shafarevich, Basic Algebraic Geometry 2, Chapter VII, Section 2), applied to the base change along σ of a geometrically integral affine variety over K.
check.note: The product topology on functions from A to ℂ agrees on this set with the classical topology of the complex points, because a homomorphism is determined by its values on finitely many generators of A.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.GroupCoh.isZero_tateCohomology_of_index
theorems.areas: representation theory, category theory, group theory, homological algebra

a.states: Let k be a commutative ring, G a finite group, A a k-linear representation of G, and n an integer. Suppose that for every prime p dividing the order of G there is a subgroup P of G whose index is prime to p and for which the n-th Tate cohomology of P with coefficients in the restriction of A is zero. Then the n-th Tate cohomology of G with coefficients in A is zero.
a.notation: (∀p prime, p | #G ⟹ ∃P ≤ G, p ∤ [G : P] ∧ Ĥⁿ(P, Res A) = 0) ⟹ Ĥⁿ(G, A) = 0
a.known_as: The Sylow criterion for the vanishing of Tate cohomology. It rests on the fact that restriction to a subgroup of index prime to p is injective on the p-primary component.
a.reference: Michael F. Atiyah and C. T. C. Wall, Cohomology of Groups, in J. W. S. Cassels and A. Fröhlich (eds.), Algebraic Number Theory, 1967
a.why: The usual statement asks for vanishing on the Sylow p-subgroups, while the Lean text accepts any subgroup of index prime to p, which includes the Sylow case and follows from the same restriction and corestriction argument, so the label depends on which textbook form is taken as the reference.

b.states: Let k be a commutative ring, G a finite group, A a k-linear representation of G and n an integer. Suppose that for every prime p dividing the order of G there is a subgroup P of G whose index is prime to p and for which the Tate cohomology group Ĥⁿ(P, A) of the restricted representation is zero. Then the Tate cohomology group Ĥⁿ(G, A) is zero.
b.known_as: Vanishing of Tate cohomology is detected on Sylow subgroups (Serre, Local Fields, Chapter IX, §2, and Cassels–Fröhlich, Chapter IV, §6). The proof uses the fact that restriction followed by corestriction is multiplication by the index. Here any subgroup of index prime to p takes the place of a Sylow p-subgroup
b.vacuity: None found, and for the trivial group the hypothesis is empty while the conclusion is the true vanishing of all Tate cohomology of the trivial group.

check.known_as: The Sylow criterion for the vanishing of Tate cohomology, which rests on restriction followed by corestriction being multiplication by the index (Atiyah and Wall in Cassels and Fröhlich, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter IV), here with any subgroup of index prime to p in place of a Sylow p-subgroup.
check.note: The vanishing is assumed only in the single degree n and only for one subgroup per prime, and a Sylow p-subgroup is one admissible choice among the subgroups of index prime to p.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.isRegularRing_formalFibre_of_essFiniteType
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let Λ be a regular integral domain whose fraction field is perfect, R a local ring that is essentially of finite type over Λ, and K a field that is essentially of finite type over R, with the composite map from Λ to K injective. Then R̂ ⊗_R K is a regular ring, where R̂ is the completion of R at its maximal ideal. Write 𝔭 for the kernel of R → K, a prime lying over the generic point of Spec Λ. The claim is that the formal fibre of R at 𝔭 stays regular after base change to the finitely generated field extension K of κ(𝔭).
a.notation: Λ regular domain, Frac Λ perfect, R local ess. f.t. over Λ, K field ess. f.t. over R, Λ ↪ K ⟹ R̂_𝔪 ⊗_R K regular
a.known_as: No published result known. It is a regularity statement for formal fibres lying over the generic point of a regular base, of the kind that excellence of the base would supply.
a.vacuity: None found, but in positive characteristic a regular domain with perfect fraction field must be a perfect field, so apart from that case the hypothesis amounts to a fraction field of characteristic zero.
a.why: For an excellent base such as ℤ or a field, the statement follows from geometric regularity of formal fibres (EGA IV 7.8.3), but I know no source with this hypothesis on a general regular base and its generic fibre.

b.states: Let Λ be a regular domain with perfect fraction field, R a local ring that is an essentially finite type Λ-algebra, and K a field that is an essentially finite type R-algebra. If the composite map from Λ through R to K is injective, then R̂ ⊗_R K is a regular ring, where R̂ is the completion of R at its maximal ideal. When K is a residue field of R, this says that the formal fibres of R over primes lying above the zero ideal of Λ are regular.
b.known_as: Close to Grothendieck's theorem that a ring essentially of finite type over an excellent ring is a G-ring and so has geometrically regular formal fibres (EGA IV 7.8.3, Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, §32). The Lean statement differs in two ways. Its base is only a regular domain with perfect fraction field, and it claims regularity only for fibres over the generic point of that base
b.vacuity: None found, since Λ = ℤ, R = ℤ localized at (p) and K = ℚ meet the hypotheses, although in positive characteristic a Noetherian regular domain with perfect fraction field is itself a perfect field.

check.known_as: No published result known. It is a regularity statement for the formal fibres of a local ring essentially of finite type over a regular domain at primes over the generic point of that domain, related to Grothendieck's theorem that rings essentially of finite type over an excellent ring have geometrically regular formal fibres (EGA IV 7.8.3).
check.vacuity: None found, although in positive characteristic a regular domain with perfect fraction field is itself a perfect field, so the hypothesis has real content only when the fraction field has characteristic zero.
check.note: Excellence of Λ is not assumed, and the claim is confined to fibres over the generic point of Λ, where the generic formal fibre of a regular local ring is a localization of its regular completion and the perfect fraction field keeps that regularity under the finitely generated field extension.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.dedekindZeta_eulerProduct_mul_sub_one_entire
theorems.areas: number fields, complex analysis, special functions, other analysis, topology, ring theory

a.states: For every number field K there is an entire function Z with the following property. For every complex s with real part greater than 1, Z(s) equals (s − 1) times the exponential of the sum, over the nonzero prime ideals P of the ring of integers, of −log(1 − 1·N(P)^{−s}). That exponential is the Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function, so the statement says that (s − 1)ζ_K(s) extends from the half-plane Re s > 1 to an entire function.
a.notation: ∃Z entire, ∀s with Re s > 1, Z(s) = (s − 1)·exp(∑_P −log(1 − 1·N(P)^{−s})) = (s − 1)ζ_K(s)
a.known_as: Hecke's theorem on the continuation of the Dedekind zeta function to the whole plane with at most a simple pole at s = 1
a.reference: Erich Hecke, Über die Zetafunktion beliebiger algebraischer Zahlkörper, 1917
a.why: The published theorem also gives the functional equation and the residue at s = 1, and the Lean text keeps only the entire continuation of (s − 1)ζ_K(s).

b.states: For every number field K there is an entire function Z on ℂ with the following property. For every s with real part greater than 1, Z(s) equals (s − 1) times the exponential of the sum, over the nonzero prime ideals P of the ring of integers, of −log(1 − N(P)^(−s)). That exponential is the Euler product of the Dedekind zeta function, so the claim is that (s − 1)ζ_K(s) extends from the half-plane Re s > 1 to an entire function.
b.known_as: Hecke's analytic continuation of the Dedekind zeta function to a meromorphic function on ℂ whose only pole is a simple pole at s = 1

check.known_as: Hecke's theorem on the analytic continuation of the Dedekind zeta function to a meromorphic function on ℂ whose only pole is a simple pole at s = 1.
check.note: The statement does not say that Z(1) is nonzero, so neither the existence of the pole nor its residue from the class number formula is part of it, and the functional equation is left out as well.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.function_field_class_group_powers
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let A be a Dedekind domain that is an algebra over k and over k[X], compatibly, and is finite and free as a k[X]-module. Take an integer N ≥ 2 and a nonzero maximal ideal P₀ of A. Then there is a nonzero element a of A such that the class of every nonzero maximal ideal P not containing a equals the class of P₀ times an N-th power in the class group of A.
a.notation: ∀N ≥ 2 ∀P₀ maximal ∃a ≠ 0 ∀P maximal with a ∉ P ∃d ∈ Cl(A), [P] = [P₀]·d^N
a.known_as: Divisibility of the divisor class group of a smooth affine curve over an algebraically closed field, which follows from the divisibility of the group of points of its Jacobian
a.reference: David Mumford, Abelian Varieties, 1970
a.vacuity: None found among the hypotheses, but the class group is divisible, so the conclusion already holds with a = 1 and the exceptional set that a allows is never needed.
a.why: Divisibility gives the statement at once, and the existential form with an exceptional element a looks shaped to match an argument elsewhere in the project rather than a textbook statement.

b.states: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and A a Dedekind domain that is a k-algebra and a finite free k[X]-algebra compatible with k, so that A is the coordinate ring of a smooth affine curve. Take any N ≥ 2 and any nonzero maximal ideal P₀ of A. Then there is a nonzero element a of A such that every nonzero maximal ideal P not containing a has the following property. The class of P in the ideal class group equals the class of P₀ times the N-th power of some class d.
b.known_as: Divisibility of the ideal class group of a smooth affine curve over an algebraically closed field. This class group is a quotient of the divisible group Pic⁰ of the complete curve, which is the group of points of its Jacobian
b.vacuity: The element a = 1 meets the existential claim, because the class group is divisible and every maximal ideal P therefore satisfies the conclusion, so the condition that a lies outside P does no work.

check.known_as: Divisibility of the ideal class group of a smooth affine curve over an algebraically closed field, a quotient of the divisible group of points of the Jacobian of the complete curve.
check.vacuity: No hypothesis is impossible, but a = 1 already meets the existential claim because the class group is divisible, so the condition that P avoids a does no work.
check.note: The hypothesis of characteristic zero is not needed, since the group of points of an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field is divisible in every characteristic.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.exists_basis_unique_min_and_sums_separated
theorems.areas: special functions, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let X be a free abelian group of finite rank d and q a real-valued quadratic map on X that tends to infinity along the cofinite filter, which makes q positive definite. Let g, N, N′ and D be natural numbers with d ≤ g, 1 + 2g·2^{g/2} < N and 2D·(g·(3/2)^g·2^{g/2−1})·N < N′. Then X has a basis e₁,…,e_d such that each e_i and each −e_i is the unique strict minimizer of q in its coset modulo NX. In addition, for every k ≤ D and all families α₁,…,α_k and β₁,…,β_k whose members minimize q in their cosets modulo NX, an equation ∑α_j = ∑β_j + N′w forces w = 0.
a.notation: ∃ basis e, ∀i ∀μ ≠ 0, q(±e_i) < q(±e_i + Nμ), and ∀k ≤ D ∀α, β ∈ X^k with q(α_j) ≤ q(α_j + Nw), q(β_j) ≤ q(β_j + Nw) ∀j ∀w, ∑α_j = ∑β_j + N′w ⟹ w = 0
a.known_as: No published result known. It is a lattice reduction lemma with explicit constants that separates the coset minimizers of a positive definite quadratic form.
a.why: The constants are made to measure and the combination of conditions is unusual, which points to an auxiliary lemma for a degeneration argument rather than a published statement.

b.states: Let X be a free abelian group of finite rank d and q a real-valued quadratic form on X that tends to infinity off finite sets. Let g, N, N′ and D be natural numbers with d ≤ g, N > 1 + 2g·2^(g/2) and N′ > 2D·g·(3/2)^g·2^(g/2 − 1)·N. Then there is a ℤ-basis e₁, …, e_d of X such that each e_i and each −e_i is the unique strict minimum of q on its coset modulo NX. Furthermore, let α and β be families of k ≤ D vectors in which each vector minimizes q on its coset modulo NX, and suppose Σα = Σβ + N′w. Then the vector w is zero.
b.known_as: no published result known
b.vacuity: None found, although the clause about −e_i repeats the clause about e_i because q(−x) = q(x), and the clause about sums does not involve the basis.

check.known_as: No published result known. It is a lattice reduction lemma with explicit constants that makes basis vectors unique coset minimizers of a positive definite quadratic form and separates sums of coset minimizers.
check.vacuity: None found, although the clause on −e_i repeats the clause on e_i because q(−x) = q(x).
check.note: The sum clause does not involve the basis and follows in a few lines from the bound |polar q (α_j) w| ≤ N·q(w) that every coset minimizer satisfies, which gives w = 0 as soon as N′ > D·N, far below the stated bound on N′.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.exists_basis_unique_min_pair_sums
theorems.areas: special functions, linear algebra, ring theory

a.states: Let X be a free abelian group of finite rank d and q a real-valued quadratic map on X that tends to infinity along the cofinite filter. If d ≤ g and 1 + 4g·2^{g/2} < N, then X has a basis e₁,…,e_d such that q(e_i) < q(e_i + Nμ) and q(e_i + e_j) < q(e_i + e_j + Nμ) for all indices i and j and every nonzero μ in X. So each basis vector and each sum of two basis vectors, 2e_i included, is the unique strict minimizer of q in its coset modulo NX.
a.notation: d ≤ g, 1 + 4g·2^{g/2} < N ⟹ ∃ basis e, ∀i, j ∀μ ≠ 0, q(e_i) < q(e_i + Nμ) ∧ q(e_i + e_j) < q(e_i + e_j + Nμ)
a.known_as: No published result known. It is a lattice reduction lemma with explicit constants that makes basis vectors and their pairwise sums unique coset minimizers of a positive definite quadratic form.
a.why: The explicit bound on N and the particular sums e_i + e_j are made for one construction, and I know no source that states them.

b.states: Let X be a free abelian group of finite rank d and q a real-valued quadratic form on X that tends to infinity off finite sets. Let g and N be natural numbers with d ≤ g and N > 1 + 4g·2^(g/2). Then there is a ℤ-basis e₁, …, e_d of X such that q(e_i) < q(e_i + Nμ) and q(e_i + e_j) < q(e_i + e_j + Nμ) for all indices i and j and every nonzero μ in X. So each basis vector, and each sum of two basis vectors including 2e_i, is the unique minimum of q on its coset modulo NX.
b.known_as: no published result known

check.known_as: No published result known. It is a lattice reduction lemma with explicit constants that makes basis vectors and their pairwise sums unique coset minimizers of a positive definite quadratic form.
check.note: Positive definiteness of q is not stated as a hypothesis but follows from the condition that q tends to infinity along the cofinite filter.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.adic_completion_reduced_of_jacobson
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let D be an integral domain that is essentially of finite type over ℤ, and let J be an ideal of D contained in the Jacobson radical of D. Then the J-adic completion of D is a reduced ring.
a.notation: D domain ess. f.t. over ℤ, J ⊆ Jac(D) ⟹ lim_n D/Jⁿ is reduced
a.known_as: The completion of a reduced excellent ring is reduced. Here it is applied to domains essentially of finite type over ℤ, which are excellent.
a.reference: Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné, Éléments de géométrie algébrique IV, seconde partie, 1965 (Scholie 7.8.3)
a.vacuity: None found, though for D of finite type over ℤ the Jacobson radical is zero, so J must be zero and the completion is D itself, and the content lies in localizations such as local rings of arithmetic varieties.
a.why: The conclusion follows from the excellence of D and the regularity of its completion maps, but the published scholium is phrased for semilocal completions, and the hypothesis on J suggests a formulation tied to one use.

b.states: Let D be a domain that is essentially of finite type over ℤ and J an ideal of D contained in the Jacobson radical of D. Then the J-adic completion of D is a reduced ring.
b.known_as: Reducedness of completions of reduced excellent rings (EGA IV 7.8.3 and Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, §32), which applies because rings essentially of finite type over ℤ are excellent
b.vacuity: None found, since D = ℤ localized at (p) with J = (p) meets the hypotheses, while for a finitely generated ℤ-domain the Jacobson radical is zero and the conclusion is then immediate.

check.known_as: Reducedness of the completion of a reduced excellent ring (EGA IV, Scholie 7.8.3, and Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Section 32), applied to domains essentially of finite type over ℤ, which are excellent.
check.vacuity: None found, although for a domain of finite type over ℤ the Jacobson radical is zero, so J = 0 and the completion is D itself, and the content lies in localizations such as ℤ localized at (p).
check.note: The condition that J lies in the Jacobson radical makes the completion map faithfully flat, so the reducedness comes from the regularity of the completion map of an excellent ring.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.schwartzSubmodule_eq_top_of_gaussian_mem_derivStable
theorems.areas: complex analysis, inner product spaces, Fourier analysis, other analysis, topology, linear algebra

a.states: Let V be a finite-dimensional real normed space, N a complex linear subspace of the Schwartz space S(V, ℂ), and Q a continuous real-bilinear complex-valued form on V with c‖x‖² ≤ Re Q(x, x) for some c > 0. Suppose that N contains the Schwartz function g(x) = exp(−Q(x, x)), contains the directional derivative of each of its members in each direction v, and contains ℓ(x)f(x) for each of its members f and each real linear functional ℓ. Then N is dense in the Schwartz space.
a.notation: e^{−Q(x,x)} ∈ N, ∂_v N ⊆ N, ℓ·N ⊆ N ⟹ closure(N) = S(V, ℂ)
a.known_as: Density of the Hermite functions, the polynomial multiples of a Gaussian, in the Schwartz space
a.reference: Michael Reed and Barry Simon, Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics I. Functional Analysis, revised edition, 1980 (Section V.3)
a.vacuity: None found, though closure under derivatives is not needed, because N contains every polynomial multiple of the Gaussian by the multiplication hypothesis and these are already dense.
a.why: The real Gaussian case is the classical Hermite density, the Lean text allows a complex Gaussian with positive definite real part, which the same Fourier argument covers, and the unneeded derivative hypothesis suggests a statement shaped for one application.

b.states: Let V be a finite-dimensional real normed space and N a complex subspace of the Schwartz space S(V, ℂ). Suppose N contains a Schwartz function g with g(x) = exp(−Q(x, x)), where Q is a continuous real-bilinear complex-valued form with Re Q(x, x) ≥ c‖x‖² for some c > 0. If N is closed under every directional derivative and under multiplication by every real linear functional, then N is dense in the Schwartz space.
b.known_as: Density in the Schwartz space of the Hermite functions, which are polynomials times a Gaussian. Here the Gaussian may be any exp(−Q(x, x)) with positive definite real part

check.known_as: Density of the Hermite functions, the polynomial multiples of a Gaussian, in the Schwartz space, here with a complex Gaussian whose real part is positive definite.
check.note: The hypothesis of closure under directional derivatives is superfluous, because closure under multiplication by linear functionals already puts every polynomial multiple of the Gaussian into N, and these multiples are dense also for a complex Gaussian with positive definite real part.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.idealCharacter_LSeries_continuation
theorems.areas: number fields, complex analysis, inner product spaces, special functions, other analysis, topology, ring theory

a.states: Let K be a number field and 𝔪 a nonzero ideal of its ring of integers. Let X be a multiplicative function on ideals that vanishes on the zero ideal and on every ideal not coprime to 𝔪 and has modulus 1 on every nonzero ideal coprime to 𝔪. Let φ be a multiplicative function on the mixed space ℝ^{r₁} × ℂ^{r₂} that is invariant under positive real scaling and is smooth and of modulus 1 where the norm is nonzero, and assume X((β)) = φ(β) for every nonzero integer β with β − 1 in 𝔪. Then there is an entire function Z with Z(s) = (s − 1)∑_I X(I)N(I)^{−s} for Re s > 1, and Z(1) = 0 whenever X takes a value other than 1 on some nonzero ideal coprime to 𝔪.
a.notation: X unitary Hecke character mod 𝔪 with infinity type φ ⟹ ∃Z entire, Z(s) = (s − 1)L(s, X) for Re s > 1, and (∃J ≠ 0, J + 𝔪 = 𝒪_K, X(J) ≠ 1) ⟹ Z(1) = 0
a.known_as: Hecke's theorem on the analytic continuation of L-functions of Hecke characters (Größencharaktere), which are entire for nontrivial characters
a.reference: Erich Hecke, Eine neue Art von Zetafunktionen und ihre Beziehungen zur Verteilung der Primzahlen (Zweite Mitteilung), 1920
a.why: The hypotheses describe exactly the unitary Hecke characters of modulus 𝔪 whose infinity type is trivial on positive scalars, and the conclusion keeps only the continuation and the regularity at s = 1 from Hecke's theorem, without the functional equation.

b.states: Let K be a number field and m a nonzero ideal of its ring of integers. Let X be a completely multiplicative function on ideals with X(0) = 0, of modulus one on nonzero ideals coprime to m and zero on ideals not coprime to m. Let φ be a multiplicative function on the mixed space ℝ^{r₁} × ℂ^{r₂} that is invariant under positive real scaling and is smooth and of modulus one where the norm is nonzero, with X((β)) = φ(β) for every nonzero algebraic integer β ≡ 1 mod m. Then there is an entire function Z with Z(s) = (s − 1) Σ_I X(I) N(I)^(−s) for Re s > 1, and Z(1) = 0 whenever X takes a value other than 1 on some nonzero ideal coprime to m, so the L-series of such a nontrivial Hecke character is entire.
b.known_as: Hecke's theorem on the analytic continuation of Hecke L-functions of Größencharaktere, which are entire for a nontrivial character and have at most a simple pole at s = 1 for the trivial one
b.vacuity: None found, since the trivial character modulo m with φ = 1 meets every hypothesis, and the scaling invariance of φ is what excludes characters such as N(I)^(it), whose L-series has a pole away from s = 1.

check.known_as: Hecke's theorem on the analytic continuation of the L-functions of Hecke characters (Größencharaktere), which are entire for a nontrivial character and have at most a simple pole at s = 1 for the trivial one.
check.note: The scaling invariance of φ excludes the twists by N(I)^{it}, whose L-series has its pole at 1 + it, and the functional equation is not part of the statement.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.Global.index_range_powMonoidHom_adicCompletion_mul_norm
theorems.areas: number fields, other analysis, ring theory, group theory

a.states: Let K be a number field and n a positive integer such that K contains a primitive n-th root of unity, and let v be a finite place of K with completion K_v. Then the index of the subgroup of n-th powers in K_v^×, times the norm of n in K_v, equals n². The norm on K_v has to be the normalized absolute value for this equation to hold.
a.known_as: The index formula for n-th powers in a p-adic field, [F^× : F^{×n}] = n·#μ_n(F)/|n|_F, in the case where the n-th roots of unity lie in the field
a.reference: Jürgen Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, 1999 (Chapter II, Section 5)
a.why: When K contains μ_n, the completion also contains them, so #μ_n(K_v) = n and the general formula becomes the product form in the Lean text.

b.states: Let K be a number field and n a positive integer such that K contains n distinct n-th roots of unity. For every finite place v of K, take the index of the subgroup of n-th powers in the unit group of the completion K_v and multiply it by the absolute value ‖n‖_v of n in K_v. The product equals n².
b.known_as: The index formula for n-th powers in a nonarchimedean local field, which says that the index of K_v^{×n} in K_v^× is n · #μ_n(K_v) / |n|_v (Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter II, §5). Here it appears in the case where K already contains the n-th roots of unity

check.known_as: The index formula for n-th powers in a nonarchimedean local field F, which says that the index of F^{×n} in F^× is n·#μ_n(F)/|n|_F (Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter II, Section 5), in the case where the n-th roots of unity lie in K.
check.note: Because the formula is proved, the norm that Mathlib puts on the completion must be the normalized absolute value, for which the norm of n is the absolute norm of v raised to minus the valuation of n.

theorems.name: GroundTheory.Global.index_range_powMonoidHom_adicCompletion

a.states: Let K be a number field, v a finite place of K with completion K_v, and n a nonzero natural number. Then the index of the subgroup of n-th powers in K_v^× equals n times the number of n-th roots of unity in K_v, divided by the norm of n in K_v.
a.known_as: The index formula for n-th powers in a p-adic field
a.reference: Jürgen Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, 1999 (Chapter II, Section 5)
a.why: By Krasner's lemma the completions of number fields at finite places are exactly the finite extensions of the fields ℚ_p, and the Lean formula is the textbook one with the normalized absolute value.

b.states: Let K be a number field, v a finite place and n a nonzero natural number. Then the index of the subgroup of n-th powers in the unit group K_v^× of the completion equals n times the number of n-th roots of unity in K_v, divided by the absolute value ‖n‖_v of n in K_v.
b.known_as: The index formula for n-th powers in a nonarchimedean local field, which says that the index of K_v^{×n} in K_v^× is n · #μ_n(K_v) / |n|_v (Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter II, §5)

check.known_as: The index formula for n-th powers in a nonarchimedean local field F, which says that the index of F^{×n} in F^× is n·#μ_n(F)/|n|_F (Neukirch, Algebraic Number Theory, Chapter II, Section 5).
check.note: The index is a natural number cast to ℝ that Mathlib sets to zero for an infinite index, so the formula also shows that the index is finite.

theorems.name: GlobalTheory.T.primitive_derivation_pairing
theorems.areas: linear algebra, ring theory, field theory

a.states: Let k be an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic p, and let A be a finite-dimensional commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebra over k, which is the coordinate ring of a finite commutative group scheme over k. Let P be a subspace of A made of primitive elements, those f with Δf = f ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ f. Let W be a subspace of the dual of A made of functionals v with v(fg) = v(f)ε(g) + ε(f)v(g), which are elements of the Lie algebra of the group scheme. If every element of W vanishes on every element of P, then p^{dim P + dim W} divides dim_k A.
a.notation: P ⊆ Prim(A), W ⊆ Der_ε(A, k), W(P) = 0 ⟹ p^{dim P + dim W} | dim_k A
a.known_as: No published result known. It is a divisibility bound for the order of a finite commutative group scheme in terms of an orthogonal pair of subspaces, one of primitive elements and one of Lie algebra elements.
a.why: Under Cartier duality, the primitive elements of A form the Lie algebra of the dual group scheme and the counit derivations form the Lie algebra of the group scheme itself, and I know no source that states this divisibility for an orthogonal pair of subspaces.

b.states: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0 and A a finite-dimensional commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebra over k. Let P be a subspace of primitive elements of A, and let W be a subspace of linear forms on A that are derivations at the counit and that all vanish on P. Then p^(dim P + dim W) divides dim A. In terms of the finite commutative group scheme G = Spec A, P lies in the Lie algebra of the Cartier dual of G and W lies in the Lie algebra of G, and the two subspaces are orthogonal under the natural pairing.
b.known_as: no published result known

check.known_as: No published result known. It is a divisibility bound for the order of a finite commutative group scheme over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p in terms of an orthogonal pair of subspaces of the Lie algebra of the group scheme and of the Lie algebra of its Cartier dual.
check.note: The orthogonality hypothesis is needed, as α_p shows, where the primitive element x and the derivation at the counit pair to 1 and the sum of dimensions 2 would give p² dividing p.

theorems.name: UpperTheory.V.J.htPres
theorems.areas: ring theory

a.states: Let O be a discrete valuation ring that is complete for its maximal ideal, N and N′ natural numbers, R a commutative ring, and p a surjective ring homomorphism from the power series ring O[[x₁,…,x_N]] onto R whose kernel is generated by N′ power series f₁,…,f_{N′}. Then every prime ideal Q of R satisfies two relations for its preimage 𝔮 = p⁻¹(Q). The height of 𝔮 plus the Krull dimension of R/Q equals N + 1, and the height of 𝔮 is at most the height of Q plus N′.
a.notation: ∀Q ∈ Spec R, ht(p⁻¹Q) + dim(R/Q) = N + 1 ∧ ht(p⁻¹Q) ≤ ht(Q) + N′
a.known_as: The dimension formula ht 𝔮 + dim A/𝔮 = dim A in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring, combined with the consequence of Krull's height theorem that dividing by r elements lowers the dimension by at most r, both applied to A = O[[x₁,…,x_N]]
a.reference: Hideyuki Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, 1986 (Theorems 13.6 and 17.4)
a.vacuity: None found, apart from the degenerate case in which the kernel is the whole ring and R has no prime ideals.
a.why: Both parts are textbook facts specialized to the regular local ring O[[x₁,…,x_N]] of dimension N + 1, packaged in the form used for presentations of deformation rings, so the kind is clear, but the relation has to be judged against two published results at once.

b.states: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring, and let p be a surjective ring homomorphism from the power series ring O[[x₁, …, x_N]] onto a ring R whose kernel is generated by N′ power series. Then every prime Q of R satisfies two claims. The height of the preimage of Q plus the Krull dimension of R/Q equals N + 1. The height of the preimage of Q is at most the height of Q plus N′.
b.known_as: The dimension formula ht 𝔓 + dim B/𝔓 = dim B = N + 1 in the catenary regular local domain B = O[[x₁, …, x_N]], combined with Krull's height theorem in the form ht 𝔓 ≤ ht(𝔓/I) + μ(I) for an ideal I generated by μ(I) elements (Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, §13 and §31)

check.known_as: The dimension formula ht 𝔮 + dim B/𝔮 = dim B in the regular local ring B = O[[x₁,…,x_N]] of dimension N + 1, combined with Krull's height theorem in the form that dividing by N′ elements lowers the height by at most N′ (Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorems 13.6 and 17.4).
check.note: The first relation uses only that O[[x₁,…,x_N]] is a regular local ring of dimension N + 1, and the generators of the kernel enter only the second relation.
